title: Alcoholic Ginger Beer
keywords: ginger, beer, alcoholic, homemade, beverage, fermented
ingredients: 2 1/2 cups (600 milliliters) warm, filtered (or pre-boiled) water
instructions: First thing's first: Start by making a 'plant' for your ginger beer. Stir the yeast into the water until dissolved. Add in 1 tablespoon freshly grated ginger, 1 tablespoon sugar, the lemon juice, and the sliced jalapeño, if you're using it. Stir to combine.

Pour the mixture into a glass jar -- one that's large enough for the liquid to fit comfortably, with a bit of extra space. Cover with a clean, dry kitchen towel and secure it with a rubber band. Place the jar in the warmest place in your house: next to your heater, near the refrigerator, or by a heat vent.

Every day for the next week you'll have to 'feed' your plant. First off, feel the bottle -- it should be slightly warm. Take the towel off your jar and add another tablespoon of grated ginger and another tablespoon of sugar. Stir until the sugar dissolves, then replace the towel and put your plant back in a warm place. Do this every day for a week.
After about a week, you should see small bubbles floating to the surface of your plant.

Now it's time to bottle! Estimate how much water you'll need to fill your plastic soda bottles two-thirds of the way full. Dissolve enough sugar into the water so that it tastes very sweet -- as sweet as soda.

Using a cheesecloth, strain the plant out into a large measuring cup or bowl. Next, use a funnel to add the sweetened water to the bottles until they are two-thirds of the way full. Add about a cup of the plant liquid to each clean, dry soda bottle. Stir with a chopstick to combine.
Seal the bottles tightly with their caps and put them back in the same warm place where you once kept the plant. Squeeze the bottles daily to test how they're carbonating.

After a few days, they should become difficult to compress; when they feel like a rock and are impossible to squeeze at all, slowly start to unscrew the cap just until you hear hissing, but do not open it all the way. Whenever the bottle is impossible to compress, let out the carbonation, then seal it back tightly.
In a week and a half to two weeks, the yeast should have eaten up most of the sugar in the bottle. This means your ginger beer is ready to open up and taste!
Serve ice cold with citrus wedges and a rum float if you're feeling dangerous. Make sure to consume the whole bottle within 24 hours after opening.
notes: Glass bottles could explode from carbonation, so make sure to use plastic soda bottles.

title: Fluffy American pancakes
keywords: pancakes, american, fluffy, breakfast, brunch
ingredients: 2 tbsp melted butter (allowed to cool slightly) or olive oil, plus extra for cooking
instructions: Sift the flour, baking powder, salt and caster sugar into a large bowl. In a separate bowl or jug, lightly whisk together the milk and egg, then whisk in the melted butter.
Pour the milk mixture into the flour mixture and, using a fork, beat until you have a smooth batter. Any lumps will soon disappear with a little mixing. Let the batter stand for a few minutes.

Heat a non-stick frying pan over a medium heat and add a knob of butter. When it's melted, add a ladle of batter (or two if your frying pan is big enough to cook two pancakes at the same time). It will seem very thick but this is how it should be. Wait until the top of the pancake begins to bubble, then turn it over and cook until both sides are golden brown and the pancake has risen to about 1 cm / 1/2 in thick.
Repeat until all the batter is used up. You can keep the pancakes warm in a low oven, but they taste best fresh out the pan.
Serve with lashings of real maple syrup and extra butter, if you like.
notes: For extra-fluffy pancakes substitute self-raising flour for plain flour and still use the baking powder.

title: Apple & cranberry sauce
keywords: apple, cranberry, sauce, christmas, jamie oliver
ingredients: 500 g cranberries, fresh cranberries or frozen ones, thawed
2 bramley apples, peeled, cored and cut into chunks
instructions: This is a simple sauce that goes very well with rich meats like goose and duck. You can make it well in advance, so you don't have to worry about it while you're cooking lunch. Pop some in a sterilised jar as a lovely home-made Christmas gift that's sure to impress.

Place all the ingredients in a wide saucepan and add a splash of water. Put the pan on the heat and bring to the boil. Simmer gently until the cranberries have burst and the apple has softened. Boil down until the mixture thickens slightly, then take off the heat and leave to cool.
If giving as a gift, divide between air-tight sterilised jars and give out to all your friends. Once opened, store in the fridge.
notes: Goes very well with rich meats like goose and duck.

title: Flat apple & vanilla tart
keywords: apple, tart, vanilla, baking, puff pastry
ingredients: 5 large eating apples - Cox's, russets or Elstar
3 tsp vanilla sugar or 1 tsp vanilla extract
instructions: Heat oven to 220C/fan 200C/gas 7. Roll out the pastry and trim to a round about 35cm across. Transfer to a baking sheet lined with parchment paper.
Peel, core and thinly slice the apples and toss in the lemon juice. Spread over the pastry to within 2cm of the edges. Curl up the edges slightly to stop the juices running off.
Dot the top with the butter and sprinkle with vanilla and caster sugar. Bake for 15-20 mins until the apples are tender and the pastry crisp.
Warm the conserve and brush over the apples and pastry edge. Serve hot with vanilla ice cream or crème fraîche.
notes: Serve hot with vanilla ice cream or crème fraîche.

title: Banana bread
keywords: banana, bread, cake, baking, sweet
ingredients: 85ml/3fl oz buttermilk (or normal milk mixed with 1 1/2 tsp lemon juice or vinegar)
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180C/350F/Gas 4.
Sift the flour, bicarbonate of soda and salt into a large mixing bowl.
In a separate bowl, cream the butter and sugar together until light and fluffy.
Add the eggs, mashed bananas, buttermilk and vanilla extract to the butter and sugar mixture and mix well. Fold in the flour mixture.
Grease a 20cm x 12.5cm/8in x 5in loaf tin (2lb) and pour the cake mixture into the tin.
Transfer to the oven and bake for about an hour, or until well-risen and golden-brown.
Remove from the oven and cool in the tin for a few minutes, then turn out onto a wire rack to cool completely before serving.
notes: If you don't have buttermilk, some plain yoghurt would work here.

title: Bbq pork ribs
keywords: bbq, pork, ribs, marmite, mustard, dinner
ingredients: 2 racks of baby back / loin ribs
instructions: Turn the racks curved-side down, and with the wider end facing you. Use a small knife to peel the edge of the translucent membrane away from the smaller end of the rack to form a tab you can grip on to. Pull this towards you, so the membrane comes away from the bones.

Mix together the marinade ingredients and rub about half into the ribs well. Put in a shallow dish, cover and leave in the fridge for 4 hours, turning once or twice during this time to make sure the entire rack is coated.
Pre-heat the oven to 130C. Cover the dish tightly with foil and cook for about 4 - 4½ hours until tender, basting once or twice during this time. The rack should end up floppy.
Heat a barbecue or a griddle pan until hot, then brush the ribs with the rest of the marinade and cook until charred and caramelised. Serve immediately.
notes: Baste with remaining marinade when caramelising on grill.

title: Homemade Beef Jerky
keywords: beef, jerky, snack, high protein, chef john
ingredients: 1 tablespoon smoked paprika, or to taste
1 tablespoon honey, or more to taste
2 pounds beef top round, thinly sliced
instructions: Whisk Worcestershire sauce, soy sauce, paprika, honey, black pepper, red pepper flakes, garlic powder, and onion powder together in a bowl. Add beef to bowl and turn to coat beef completely. Cover the bowl with plastic wrap and marinate in the refrigerator, 3 hours to overnight.
Preheat oven to 175 degrees F (80 degrees C). Line a baking sheet with aluminum foil and place a wire rack over the foil.
Transfer beef to paper towels to dry. Discard marinade. Arrange beef slices in a single layer on the prepared wire rack on the baking sheet.
Bake beef in the preheated oven until dry and leathery, 3 to 4 hours. Cut with scissors into bite-size pieces.
notes: Have your butcher slice the beef thinly for you.

title: Beef rendang & turmeric rice
keywords: beef, rendang, turmeric rice, curry, asian, coconut
ingredients: 2kg beef shin or skirt, cut into bite-sized cubes
thumb-sized piece galangal, peeled and chopped (for paste)
instructions: For the paste, soak the chillies in boiling water for 15 mins. Drain, remove seeds and whizz with the rest of the paste ingredients in a small food processor until smooth.

Heat the oil in a wok or a heavy-based flameproof casserole dish. Fry the paste for 5 mins until the aroma is released. Add the beef and the lemongrass, and mix well. Once the beef starts to lose its pinkness, add the coconut milk and 250ml water. Bring to the boil, then lower to a simmer, uncovered. Stir occasionally to avoid sticking, and more often towards the end.
Meanwhile, toast the coconut in a frying pan on a low heat for 5-7 mins until golden brown. Set aside to cool. Using a blender, coarsely blend it to finer pieces - but not too fine. Put to one side.

After 2 hrs, add the coconut, kaffir lime leaves, chicken stock powder, tamarind paste, sugar and salt to the pan. Simmer for 30 mins more. You should start to see the oil separating from the mix. It's ready when the meat is tender and almost falling apart.

For the rice, use a heavy-based saucepan with a lid. Heat the oil in the pan and add the mustard seeds. Once the seeds start popping, add the turmeric, curry leaves (if using) and rice, and mix well. Add the chicken stock and 1 litre of water. Bring to the boil, then turn down to the lowest simmer and cook, covered, for 5 mins. Remove from the heat, with the lid on and leave to steam for 25 mins.
notes: If galangal is unavailable, ginger can be used as a replacement.

title: The Perfect Burger
keywords: burger, beef, grill, bbq, american
ingredients: Flavour Perk Options: 1 tbsp creamy caesar/Greek dressing, 1 tbsp sun-dried tomato, 1 tbsp sour cream/yoghurt, 1 tbsp lemon/lime rind, 1 tbsp gingerroot, 1 tbsp ketchup/BBQ sauce, 1 tsp lemon pepper, 1 tsp curry powder, 1 tsp oregano/thyme/rosemary, 1 tbsp fresh herb, 2 tsp cajun seasoning, 1 tsp sesame oil, 1 tsp teriyaki/hoisin sauce, 1 fresh/pickled jalapeno pepper, chopped
instructions: Lightly oil grill & heat BBQ to medium.
Whisk egg in a bowl & add next 6 ingredients.
Add any of the 'stir-ins' that appeal to you.
Crumble in beef & using your hands or a fork, gently mix together.
Handle the meat as little as possible - the more you work it, the tougher it gets.
Gently shape (don't firmly press) mixture into burgers about 1/2 inch thick.
Using your thumb, make a shallow depression in the centre of each burger to prevent puffing up during cooking.
Place burgers on the grill, close lid & BBQ until NO LONGER PINK INSIDE, turning once, about 6 - 8 minutes per side.
An instant read thermometer should read 160F.
Don't abuse your burgers by pressing with a spatula, pricking with a fork or turning frequently as precious juices will be lost!
Tuck into a warm crusty bun & add your favourite toppings.
notes: Use medium ground beef for moistness & flavour; leaner varieties produce drier burgers.

title: Black pudding / chorizo scotch eggs
keywords: scotch eggs, black pudding, chorizo, pork, eggs, deep fry
ingredients: 400g homemade or good-quality shop-bought black pudding (for chorizo use 300g each)
Sea salt and freshly ground black pepper
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180 degrees.
Put the black pudding, minced pork, breadcrumbs and parsley into a large bowl and mix until evenly combined, seasoning well with salt and pepper. Divide the mixture into 12 even-sized balls.

Bring a pan of water to the boil, add the 6 eggs and cook for 6 minutes, which should give you a soft-set yolk. Drain the eggs and run them under the cold tap until cool enough to handle. Carefully shell them.
For the coating, set out three bowls. Put the flour into one bowl and season it with salt and pepper. Break an egg into the next and beat it lightly. Tip the coarse breadcrumbs into the third bowl.

Take two of the black pudding balls and flatten them out to rough discs, about 6cm in diameter. Place one disc in the palm of your hand, set a boiled egg in the middle, then top with the second disc. Mould the black pudding around the egg, sealing the joins well. Repeat with the remaining black pudding and eggs.

Coat each Scotch egg with seasoned flour. Next, dip it in the beaten egg (lightly beat in another egg if you need to) and finally roll it in the breadcrumbs. Chill the eggs until you’re ready to cook them.

Heat a 5–7cm depth of oil in a deep pan to 175°C, or until hot enough to turn a few breadcrumbs golden in 30–40 seconds. Cook 2 or 3 eggs at a time. Lower them into the oil and fry for 2 minutes, turning regularly until golden and crisp. Transfer to the oven and cook for 10 minutes. Drain on kitchen paper and leave to stand for 5–10 minutes before tucking in.
notes: For chorizo variation, use 300g chorizo and 300g minced pork.

title: Botham burgers - ½ original recipe
keywords: burgers, beef, whole grain, coriander, cumin, bbq
ingredients: 1 lb of good quality ground beef, preferably natural or organic
1 handful of fresh bread crumbs with crust removed (about one slice)
1 small pinch of cumin seeds, crushed
instructions: In a bowl, combine the ground beef, diced red onion, egg, and fresh breadcrumbs.
Add the crushed coriander seeds, crushed cumin seeds, and Dijon mustard.
Season generously with salt and freshly ground pepper.
Mix gently with hands until ingredients are just combined; avoid overworking the meat.
Shape into 4 equal-sized burger patties.
Grill or pan-fry to desired doneness and serve on whole grain hamburger buns.
notes: This is a half-size batch of the original Botham burgers recipe.

title: Caipirinha sorbet
keywords: sorbet, caipirinha, lime, cachaca, mint, dessert, frozen
ingredients: 2 2/3 handfuls of young mint leaves (to serve)
instructions: Heat the water and caster sugar together in a saucepan, stirring until the sugar has dissolved.
Remove from the heat and allow to cool to room temperature. Add the lime juice and Cachaça and mix well.
Churn in an ice cream machine; alternatively, pour the mixture into a large plastic bowl and freeze, beating frequently with a wooden spoon to break up the ice crystals.
Serve in tiny scoops (it is very strong) with an edible flower or sprig of mint to decorate.
notes: Recipe by Marcello Tully. Serve in tiny scoops as the alcohol makes it very strong.

title: Cambodian Chicken Amok
keywords: chicken, amok, cambodian, curry, coconut milk, lemongrass, kaffir lime
ingredients: Fresh ginger (a good chunk - about as long as your middle finger)
1/4 cup of palm sugar (or 2 pressed cubes)
A good splash of soy sauce
2 large / 3 normal chicken breasts (or equivalent fish/prawns)
A handful of green beans (or snow peas)
Optional veggies: spinach, mushrooms, asparagus, tofu, bok choy
instructions: Peel the garlic and ginger, roughly cut all the sauce ingredients and throw them into a food processor (or mortar and pestle / blender with extra oil/lime juice). Whiz up until smooth to form the curry paste.
Chop the chicken and vegetables and set aside.
Fry your curry paste in a pan for 3-4 minutes until aromatic.

Add the coconut milk and let it lightly simmer. You can add extra lemongrass and lime leaves here for stronger flavor. Simmer for 20-30 minutes, adding a dash of milk if needed to prevent over-thickening.
In another pan, fry up the chicken. Once cooked, add a splash of soy sauce, then mix the chicken into the coconut milk sauce along with your vegetables.
Let cook for a further 10-15 minutes until vegetables are ready.
Remove any extra whole lime leaves and lemongrass stalks before serving with rice.
notes: If short on time, skip extra lime leaves/lemongrass in step 4 and simmer sauce for just 5-10 minutes.

title: Chestnut stuffing roll
keywords: chestnut, stuffing, bacon, sage, hazelnuts, roast, side dish
ingredients: 2 tbsp butter, plus extra to serve (to assemble)
instructions: To make the stuffing, melt 1 tbsp butter in a large non-stick pan, add the onions and gently cook for 10-15 mins until very soft. Stir in the sage for 1 min, then tip into a large mixing bowl.
Pulse the chestnuts in a food processor until chopped into small bits, tip into the bowl with onions, and repeat with the hazelnuts.
Add breadcrumbs, mace, beaten eggs, 1 tsp salt and pepper to the bowl; mix well.

Tear off a very large sheet of foil. Smear 2 tbsp butter in the middle in a rectangle about 30x40cm. Lay bacon rashers over in an overlapping row. Roll a rolling pin down the length to stretch them slightly.
Shape stuffing into a log along the rashers. Use the foil to roll up stuffing so it's wrapped in bacon. Overwrap with extra foil, twist ends to seal, and chill until ready to roast.
To cook, bake at 200C/180C fan/gas 6 for 30 mins. Turn heat to 220C/200C fan/gas 7, unwrap stuffing and cook for 30 mins more until crisp.
Slice and serve with sage leaves fried in butter, if liked.
notes: Can be made up to 2 days ahead and stored in the fridge until ready to roast.

title: CHICKEN AND CHORIZO CASSOULET
keywords: chicken, chorizo, cassoulet, butter beans, cannellini, stew, spanish
ingredients: One large chicken breast per person
1 chorizo for every 2 people (finely sliced, skin removed)
1 large onion, peeled and finely chopped
1 can butter beans, rinsed and drained
½ to 1 can cannellini beans, drained and rinsed
Sea salt and cracked black pepper
instructions: Dust the chicken in the flour.
Heat the oil in a large pan. Add the chicken and cook to seal or slightly brown, then remove from pan and set aside.
Add the chorizo and onion to the pan and cook for 3-4 minutes until the orange oil starts to release from the chorizo.
Add the garlic, carrots, and celery and cook until softened.
Return the chicken to the pan and add the stock, tomatoes, tomato puree, bay leaves, and thyme.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low and cook covered for 30 minutes.
Add the beans, salt, and pepper, and cook on low for a further 30 minutes.
Serve hot with crusty bread.
notes: Make sure to taste before adding extra salt, as chorizo and stock can be naturally salty.

title: Simple Homemade Chicken Ramen
keywords: ramen, chicken, Japanese, soup, noodles, soft boiled egg, shiitake
ingredients: kosher salt and freshly-ground black pepper, to season
1 oz dried shiitake mushrooms (or 1/2 cup fresh)
optional: fresh jalapeño slices, for serving
instructions: Cook the chicken: Preheat oven to 375 degrees. Season chicken generously with salt and pepper. Melt butter in a large oven-safe skillet over medium heat. Add chicken skin-side down and cook 5-7 minutes until skin is golden brown. Flip and cook 4-5 minutes. Transfer skillet to oven and roast 15-20 minutes until cooked through. Remove, plate, and cover with foil.

Make the ramen broth: Heat oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add garlic and ginger, cooking a few minutes until softened. Add soy sauce and mirin, stir and cook 1 minute. Add chicken stock, cover, and bring to a boil. Remove lid, simmer uncovered for 5 minutes, then add mushrooms and simmer gently for 10 minutes. Season with sea salt to taste.

Make soft-boiled eggs: Bring a pot of water to boil. Lower cold eggs into boiling water and simmer for 7 minutes (slightly runny) or 8 minutes (soft set). Transfer eggs to an ice bath for 5 minutes, then peel and slice in half lengthwise.

Assemble ramen bowls: Slice chicken into thin pieces. Cook ramen noodles in boiling water for 2-3 minutes until soft, then divide into two large bowls. Pour over broth and chicken. Top with scallions, jalapeño (if using), and soft-boiled egg. Serve immediately.
notes: You can cut prep time in half by using a store-bought whole rotisserie chicken instead.

title: Chipotle Barbacoa Beef Burrito (Copycat)
keywords: barbacoa, beef, chipotle, copycat, mexican, slow cook, burrito
instructions: Preheat oven to 325 degrees.
Add vinegar, lime juice, chipotle, garlic, cumin, oregano, black pepper, salt, and ground cloves into a blender or food processor and process until small homogenous chunks occur.
Trim beef. Add vegetable oil to a large Dutch oven and heat on high.
Sear beef on all sides until deeply browned.
Pour spice mixture over the beef and spread evenly.
Add chicken broth along the sides of the beef so you don't wash the topping off.
Bake covered in the oven at 325 degrees for 3-4 hours until fork tender (or cook in a slow cooker on low for 7 hours).
notes: Copycat version of Chipotle Barbacoa Beef.

title: Chocolate Brownies
keywords: brownies, chocolate, dark chocolate, white chocolate, baking, dessert
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C/355°F/Gas 4.
Grease and line the sides and base of a 33cm x 23cm x 5.5cm (13in x 9in x 2in) baking tin.
Place butter and dark chocolate into a heatproof bowl over a saucepan of barely simmering water (do not let base touch water) to melt.
Whisk eggs, sugar, and vanilla extract together in a clean bowl.
Allow melted chocolate mixture to cool slightly, then whisk in the egg mixture.
Sift flour and salt together, then fold into the chocolate mixture.
Mix in the chopped white chocolate pieces.
Pour into the baking tin and bake for 25 minutes. Cool in the tin before cutting into squares.
notes: Small size variation: 188g butter, 188g dark chocolate, 3 eggs, 175g sugar, 1 dsp vanilla, 113g flour, 1/2 tsp salt. Bake in 20cm tin at 150°C for 20 minutes.

title: Chocolate butter cream
keywords: buttercream, icing, chocolate, cake, frosting, baking
servings: Fills and coats a 20cm round cake
instructions: In a small bowl, blend the cocoa powder with the boiling water until smooth, then allow to cool slightly.
In a separate bowl, beat the butter until soft and creamy.
Gradually sift and beat in the icing sugar until fully incorporated.
Add the cooled cocoa mixture and beat thoroughly until light and fluffy.
Use to fill and coat a 20cm round Victoria sandwich cake.
notes: Will fill and coat a 20cm round Victoria sandwich.

title: Slow Cooked Shredded Beef Ragu Pasta
keywords: ragu, beef, pappardelle, slow cook, Italian, chuck beef, pasta
ingredients: 2.5 lb / 1.2kg chuck beef (cut into 4 equal pieces)
1 cup / 250ml red wine (merlot or cabernet sauvignon)
3/4 tsp dried thyme or 3 sprigs fresh thyme
instructions: Pat beef dry and sprinkle with salt and pepper. Heat 1 tbsp olive oil over high heat in a heavy pot; sear beef on all sides until browned (about 3 mins total), then remove to a plate.
Lower heat to medium-low, add remaining 2 tbsp olive oil. Sauté garlic and onion for 2 minutes, then add carrots and celery and sauté slowly for 5 minutes.

Add remaining ragu ingredients (except extra salt/pepper for finishing) and return beef + juices to pot. Bring to a simmer, then turn down to low, cover, and cook for 2 hours until tender enough to shred.
Remove beef and coarsely shred with 2 forks. Return beef to pot and simmer uncovered for 30 minutes until sauce reduces and thickens.
Taste and adjust seasoning. Bring a large pot of salted water to boil, cook pappardelle 1 minute less than packet instructions.
Transfer cooked pasta directly into a large pan with 5 cups of sauce and 3/4 cup pasta water. Toss gently for 1-2 minutes to coat before serving with parmesan.
notes: Can also be made in a slow cooker on low for 6-8 hours or pressure cooker on high for 40 minutes.

title: Chocolate Guinness Cake
keywords: chocolate, guinness, cake, beer, stout, cream cheese, icing
instructions: Preheat the oven to gas mark 4/180°C/160°C fan, and butter and line a 23cm springform tin.
Pour the Guinness into a large wide saucepan, add the butter (in spoons or slices), and heat until the butter is melted.
Whisk in the cocoa powder and caster sugar.
In a separate bowl, beat the sour cream with the eggs and vanilla extract.
Pour the sour cream mixture into the pan with the buttery, beery chocolate mix.
Whisk in the plain flour and bicarbonate of soda.
Pour the cake batter into the prepared tin and bake for 45 minutes to an hour (check around 48 minutes). Leave to cool completely in the tin on a cooling rack.
For the icing, lightly whip the cream cheese until smooth, sieve over the icing sugar, and beat together (or process in a food processor).
Add the cream and beat again until it reaches a spreadable consistency, then spread over the top of the cooled cake.
notes: Leaves a very damp, moist cake texture[cite: 21]. Make sure to cool completely in the tin before topping[cite: 21].

title: Crumble Recipe
keywords: crumble, fruit crumble, oats, butter, brown sugar, baking
ingredients: Tasty fruit of choice (for the base)
instructions: Combine the unsalted butter, soft brown sugar, plain flour, wholemeal flour, and porridge oats in a bowl to form a crumbly topping.
Place your prepared fruit into a baking dish.
Spread the crumble topping evenly over the fruit.
Bake in the oven at 180°C fan for approximately 30 minutes until golden and bubbling.
notes: Place on top of any tasty fruit of choice before baking[cite: 22].

title: Daffy’s Gin & Tonic Cheese Cake
keywords: cheesecake, gin, tonic, fentimans, lime, mascarpone, no bake
ingredients: Zest of half to whole lime
instructions: Put butter and caster sugar into a heavy-based saucepan and heat gently.
Crush the digestive biscuits roughly and add to the pan, removing from heat and stirring gently.
Add the tonic water in three lots until the mixture is crumbly (you may not need all of it).
In a large bowl, gently stir the mascarpone to loosen it, then add lime juice, part of the lime zest, icing sugar, and vanilla extract.
Slowly pour in the gin while stirring, ensuring the mixture doesn't get too runny.
In another bowl, whip the double cream with the remaining lime zest into firm peaks.
Gently fold the whipped cream into the mascarpone mixture.
Press the base mixture into a dish or cling-film-lined ramekins and top with the gin cheesecake mixture. Chill in the fridge before serving.
notes: Can be set in individual ramekins lined with cling film and inverted onto plates for serving[cite: 23].

title: Easy chocolate cake
keywords: chocolate, cake, easy, sponge, baking
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C (160°C fan).
Grease and line a 20cm round cake tin.
Combine the softened butter, flour, cocoa powder, eggs, and caster sugar in a bowl and mix until smooth.
Pour the batter into the prepared tin and level the surface.
Bake for 25-30 minutes until risen and springy to the touch.
notes: Makes 1 x 20cm round cake[cite: 24].

title: GINGER HONEY ROASTED PORK TENDERLOIN
keywords: pork, tenderloin, ginger, honey, soy sauce, garlic, roast
ingredients: 1 lb pork tenderloin, excess fat trimmed
kosher salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Combine ginger, honey, lemon juice, garlic, soy sauce, cayenne, salt, and pepper in a small mixing bowl.
Add half the marinade mixture to a ziplock bag with the pork tenderloin. Seal and marinate for a few hours or overnight. Refrigerate the remaining marinade.
Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C). Line a baking sheet with a double layer of aluminum foil.
Heat a large skillet with olive oil over medium-high heat. Remove pork from marinade and sear briefly on all sides until golden brown.
Transfer tenderloin to prepared baking sheet and roast for 10-15 minutes until internal temperature reaches 133°F.
Brush with leftover marinade and broil on HIGH for 1-2 minutes until golden.
Cover with foil and let rest a few minutes until internal temperature reaches 140-145°F. Slice and serve garnished with fresh parsley.
notes: Prep time does not include marinating time[cite: 26].

title: Homemade Coleslaw
keywords: coleslaw, cabbage, carrot, mayonnaise, mustard, salad, side dish
ingredients: 1 medium cabbage (about 2 pounds), outer leaves removed
1/2 cup loosely packed fresh parsley leaves, coarsely chopped
2 tablespoons Dijon mustard or coarse ground mustard
instructions: Quarter the cabbage through the core, remove core, and finely shred the leaves.
Place shredded cabbage, shredded carrots, and chopped parsley in a very large bowl and toss to mix.
In a separate bowl, whisk together mayonnaise, apple cider vinegar, mustard, celery seeds, salt, and pepper.
Pour two-thirds of the dressing over the cabbage and carrot mixture and toss well to coat.
Add more dressing if needed. Serve immediately or chill in the refrigerator for an hour to let flavors meld.
notes: You can use green, red, savoy, or Napa cabbage[cite: 27].

title: Honey and Rye Sourdough Loaf
keywords: sourdough, bread, rye, honey, baking, loaf
ingredients: 80 g sourdough leaven (ripe, equal parts flour and water)
instructions: Mix water and milk; reserve 20ml and stir salt into reserved liquid. Dissolve honey into the remaining liquid.
Whisk ripe leaven into the honey-milk-water mixture.
Slowly add rye flour and white bread flour to liquid to form a rough dough. Leave for 1 hour.
Sprinkle salt liquid over dough. Stretch and fold 5-6 times. Leave to rise for 4-6 hours until spongy and expanded.
Shape into a loaf, rest for 10-15 minutes, then place seam-side up into a rye-floured banneton. Prove for 1-2 hours.
Bake in a preheated oven at 220°C/Gas mark 7 with a dish of boiling water for 25 minutes.
Turn down to 200°C/Gas mark 6 for 20 minutes until it sounds hollow when tapped on the bottom. Cool completely.
notes: Addition of white flour makes rye dough easier to handle[cite: 28].

title: Honey Dijon Pork Tenderloin
keywords: pork, tenderloin, honey, dijon, soy sauce, roast, american
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F. Spray a rimmed baking sheet with cooking spray and place tenderloins on top.
Whisk together soy sauce, honey, olive oil, orange juice, dijon mustard, garlic, rosemary, and black pepper.
Cut small slits about halfway through the top of each tenderloin (about 6 slits per tenderloin) and pour sauce over.
Bake for 40-50 minutes, spooning pan sauce over meat every 10 minutes, until internal temperature reaches 145°F.
Rest 10-15 minutes before slicing and serving with pan juices.
notes: Resting time: 10 minutes[cite: 29].

title: J Sheekey's fish pie
keywords: fish pie, cod, salmon, smoked haddock, mash, British, seafood
ingredients: 125g boneless cod fillet, skinned and cut in 3cm chunks
125g boneless salmon fillet, skinned and cut in 3cm chunks
125g smoked haddock, skinned and cut in 3cm chunks
500g floury potatoes, peeled, cooked and mashed
instructions: Boil and mash the potatoes.
Poach cod, salmon, and haddock in simmering fish stock and white wine for 2 minutes, then drain and set stock liquid aside.
Melt 25g butter in a pan, stir in 25g flour, then gradually whisk in drained stock/wine liquid. Simmer 10 minutes to thicken.
Add double cream and simmer 10 minutes more. Stir in mustard, Worcestershire sauce, salt, and pepper.
Fold poached fish, chopped hard-boiled egg, and parsley into sauce. Spoon into pie dish.
Top with a layer of peas, then spread mashed potato on top and rake with a fork.
Bake at 180°C/gas 4 for 30 minutes. Scatter breadcrumbs and Parmesan on top, then bake 15 minutes more until golden.
notes: Famous classic London fish pie recipe[cite: 30].

title: KERALA EGG PUFFS
keywords: egg puffs, kerala, puff pastry, hard boiled egg, curry leaves, masala, snack
ingredients: 4 Hard boiled eggs, cut into half
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C for 10 minutes before baking and line a baking sheet with foil or parchment paper.
Heat coconut oil in a wide pan and cook sliced onions until golden brown.
Add crushed ginger and garlic and cook for 2-3 minutes.
Add turmeric, chilli powder, coriander powder, pepper powder, garam masala, and salt. Cook until oil appears (2-3 mins).
Add 1-2 tbsp hot water, tomato ketchup, and curry leaves. Mix well and remove from heat.
Thaw puff pastry squares. Beat 1 egg with 1-2 tsp water for egg wash and apply along four sides of each pastry square.
Place 1 tbsp masala on each pastry square, followed by half a hard-boiled egg and a bit more masala on top.
Bring diagonally opposite corners together and seal securely. Apply egg wash over sealed puffs.
Bake in preheated oven for 20-25 minutes until golden brown. Serve with tomato ketchup.
notes: Masala can be prepared 1-2 days in advance and refrigerated[cite: 31]. Can substitute 1 sliced tomato + 1/2-1 tsp vinegar for ketchup[cite: 31].

title: Jerk chicken with rice & peas
keywords: jerk chicken, rice and peas, scotch bonnet, coconut milk, kidney beans, caribbean
ingredients: 1 big bunch spring onions, roughly chopped
1/2 tsp dried thyme (or 1 tbsp thyme leaves)
instructions: Combine marinade ingredients (spring onions, ginger, garlic, onion, scotch bonnets, thyme, lime juice, soy sauce, oil, brown sugar, allspice, 1 tsp salt) in a food processor and blend into a thick paste.
Slash chicken thighs, rub marinade into crevices, cover and leave to marinate overnight in the fridge.
To oven roast: preheat oven to 180°C/160°C fan/gas 4. Place chicken in a roasting tin with lime halves and cook for 45 minutes until cooked through.
To barbecue: cook over slow indirect heat with wood chips for 30 minutes.

For rice & peas: rinse basmati rice and combine in a pan with coconut milk, sliced spring onions, thyme sprigs, chopped garlic, ground allspice, salt, and 300ml cold water. Bring to boil, reduce to medium, cover, and cook for 10 minutes.
Add kidney beans to rice, cover, remove from heat, and let sit for 5 minutes until liquid is absorbed.
Squeeze roasted lime over chicken and serve alongside rice & peas and hot sauce.
notes: Marinate overnight in the fridge for full flavor development[cite: 32].

title: RAAN (Leg of Lamb Marinated in Spiced Yogurt and Roasted)
keywords: raan, leg of lamb, indian, marinated, roasted, spices, yogurt, almonds, saffron
ingredients: 1 x 3kg / 6lb leg of lamb, trimmed of fat
125g / 4oz fresh root ginger, peeled and chopped
1/2 tsp saffron threads, soaked in 2 tbsp boiling water
instructions: Prick leg of lamb all over and make several deep gashes in flesh; place in a large deep roasting pan.
Blend ginger, garlic, lemon rind and juice, cumin seeds, cardamom seeds, cloves, turmeric, chilli powder, and salt to a purée.
Spread spice purée all over the lamb and set aside for 1 hour.
Blend almonds, 2 tbsp brown sugar, and half the yogurt into a purée. Stir in remaining yogurt.
Spread almond-yogurt mixture all over lamb on top of spice purée. Cover and refrigerate for 48 hours.
Bring lamb to room temperature and sprinkle with remaining 2 tbsp brown sugar.
Roast uncovered in a preheated oven at 220°C (Gas Mark 7) for 20 minutes.
Reduce temperature to 180°C (Gas Mark 4) and roast for 1 hour.
Reduce temperature to 170°C (Gas Mark 3), cover pan, and roast for 4 hours, basting occasionally.
Wrap lamb in foil and keep warm in oven. Skim excess fat from roasting pan, stir in soaked saffron mixture, and boil pan juices over high heat for 15-20 minutes until reduced by half.
Discard foil, carve lamb, and serve topped with reduced saffron sauce.
notes: Requires 48 hours chilling time in refrigerator after marinating[cite: 34].

title: Lasagne
keywords: lasagne, beef, pork, ragu, white sauce, pasta, baked, jamie oliver
instructions: Chop rosemary and bacon. Fry in 1 tbsp oil in a large casserole pan for 2 minutes.
Add minced beef and pork, cooking for 10+ minutes until liquid evaporates.
Grate carrots, onions, and celery in food processor and add to pan. Cook 15-20 minutes until softened.
Stir in tomato purée, plum tomatoes, and 4 tinfuls of water. Simmer on low for 2 hours until reduced.
For white sauce: cook sliced leeks with 2 tbsp oil and bay leaves for 30 minutes until soft.
Stir in flour, then gradually add milk while stirring. Bring to boil, simmer 5-10 mins until thick, then blitz in food processor until smooth.
Mix half grated Cheddar and half grated nutmeg into white sauce.
Preheat oven to 190°C/375°F/gas 5. Freeze half the ragù for another meal.
Assemble: layer 1/4 ragù, 1/4 white sauce, and lasagne sheets in a deep 25x30cm dish. Repeat 3 times, ending with white sauce.
Top with remaining cheese and bake for 45 minutes until golden and bubbling. Rest 5-10 minutes before serving.
notes: Makes a double batch of ragù so half can be frozen flat for later[cite: 35].

title: Mexican tortilla bake
keywords: mexican, tortilla bake, beef mince, mascarpone, mozzarella, cheddar, mary berry
ingredients: 1 mild red chilli, deseeded and finely chopped
Salt and freshly ground black pepper
instructions: Preheat oven to 160°C/140°C Fan/Gas 3.
Fry onions in oil for 3 minutes, add mince and brown meat.
Add chilli, red pepper, garlic, cumin, and coriander; fry for 5 minutes until dry.
Stir in tomato purée, mango chutney, tinned tomatoes, salt, and pepper. Cover, bring to boil, and bake in oven for 1 hour.
Remove from oven, stir in half chopped coriander, and increase oven temp to 200°C/180°C Fan/Gas 6.
Spread 1/3 of mince in baking dish, top with 1 tortilla, 1/3 mascarpone, 1/3 mozzarella, and 1/3 cheddar. Repeat twice to form 3 layers.
Bake for 25 minutes until golden-brown and bubbling. Garnish with remaining coriander.
notes: Recipe by Mary Berry[cite: 36]. Can assemble up to 6 hours ahead or freeze uncooked[cite: 36].

title: Millionaire’s Shortbread
keywords: millionaires shortbread, caramel, shortbread, chocolate, traybake, sweet
instructions: Cream butter, lard, and icing sugar together.
Add plain flour, rice flour/farola, cornflour, and salt; press into toffee tins.
Bake shortbread base for 1¼ hours at 170°C.
For caramel: combine butter, caster sugar, golden syrup, and condensed milk in a pan. Boil at 220°C for 5-10 minutes while stirring.
Pour caramel over cooled shortbread base.
Melt 170g chocolate and spread evenly over caramel layer; let set before slicing.
notes: Makes two full trays of shortbread[cite: 37].

title: HOME-MADE CHRISTMAS MINCEMEAT
keywords: mincemeat, christmas, apples, raisins, sultanas, brandy, spice, delia smith
ingredients: 450g Bramley apples, cored and chopped small
225g whole mixed candied peel, finely chopped
Grated zest and juice of 2 oranges
Grated zest and juice of 2 lemons
instructions: Combine all ingredients except brandy in a large bowl, stirring thoroughly.
Cover with a clean cloth and leave in a cool place overnight or for 12 hours.
Preheat oven to 110°C / 225°F / gas mark ¼.
Cover bowl loosely with foil and bake in oven for 3 hours, then remove.
As it cools, stir occasionally to allow the fat to coat all ingredients.
Once completely cold, stir in brandy.
Pack into sterilised jars, top with waxed discs, seal, and store in a cool, dark cupboard.
notes: Recipe by Delia Smith[cite: 38]. Keeps for up to 3 years in a cool cupboard[cite: 38]. Vegetarian suet can be used[cite: 38].

title: Mince pies shortcrust pastry
keywords: shortcrust pastry, mince pies, pastry, butter, baking
instructions: Sift plain flour and a pinch of salt into a bowl.
Rub in cold cubed butter with your fingers until mixture resembles breadcrumbs.
Stir in caster sugar, then add egg yolk and mix quickly with a palette knife.
Add 1-2 tbsp cold water a little at a time until dough draws together into a ball.
Wrap dough in cling film and chill in fridge for at least 10 minutes before rolling out for mince pies.
notes: Makes 315g pastry, perfect for 12 mince pies[cite: 39].

title: Mixed Spice
keywords: mixed spice, spice blend, allspice, cinnamon, nutmeg, mace, cloves, coriander, ginger
instructions: Combine all ground spices together in a bowl.
Mix thoroughly until completely blended.
Transfer to an airtight glass jar and store away from light and heat.
notes: Essential spice blend for British holiday baking and mincemeat[cite: 38, 40].

title: Nutella Stuffed Double Chocolate Muffins
keywords: muffins, nutella, double chocolate, chocolate chips, baking, sweet
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C/400°F/Gas 6. Grease a 12-hole muffin pan very well.
Whisk together flour, cocoa powder, sugar, baking powder, baking soda, and salt in a large bowl. Fold in chocolate chips.
In a separate bowl, whisk together egg, buttermilk, vegetable oil, and vanilla extract.
Pour wet ingredients into dry ingredients and mix until just combined (do not overmix; batter will be thick and lumpy).
Divide half of the batter evenly among the 12 muffin cups.
Spoon 1-2 teaspoons of Nutella into the center of each, then top with remaining batter.
Bake for 15-17 minutes until a toothpick inserted off-center comes out clean.
Cool in pan for 10 minutes, then transfer to a wire rack to cool completely.
notes: Homemade buttermilk shortcut: add 1 tbsp lemon juice or white vinegar to 1 cup milk and let stand 5-10 minutes[cite: 41].

title: AUTHENTIC SPANISH PAELLA
keywords: paella, spanish, bomba rice, rabbit, chorizo, shrimp, saffron, seafood
ingredients: 3 cups bomba or calasparra rice (or arborio)
4 links chorizo sausages, sliced into 1-inch pieces
instructions: Coat bottom of paella pan with olive oil over high heat. Brown chorizo slices for 1-2 minutes; set aside.
Brown seasoned rabbit pieces for 2-3 minutes; set aside.
Sauté garlic, onion, and bell pepper until soft, adding diced plum tomatoes shortly before finished.
Push vegetables to side of pan, add tomato paste to other side, and caramelize for 1-2 minutes.
Mix vegetables, meats, caramelized tomato paste, paprika, parsley, and thyme together.
Add rice and stir while browning (1-1.5 mins), crumbling in the saffron with your fingers.
Pour in enough warm chicken stock to cover mixture. Bring to steady boil over medium heat.
Cook without stirring for 10-20 minutes, adding stock as needed until top rice is al dente.
Lay shrimp on top during final 8 minutes of cooking, turning after 2-4 minutes.
Remove from heat, cover, and let rest for 15-20 minutes before serving garnished with lemon wedges.
notes: Patience is key: do not stir during the final cooking stage to achieve the classic 'socarrat' crust at the bottom[cite: 42].

title: Paprika pork
keywords: paprika pork, pork fillet, mushrooms, smoked paprika, soured cream, quick dinner
ingredients: 400g pork fillet, trimmed and cut into thick strips
Egg noodles, tagliatelle or rice (to serve)
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large pan and fry sliced onions for 10 minutes until soft and golden.
Add pork strips and sliced mushrooms; cook on high heat for 3-4 minutes until browned.
Add smoked paprika and cook for 1 minute.
Stir in tomato purée and chicken stock, then simmer for 5-8 minutes until pork is cooked through.
Mix in soured cream and seasoning. Serve over egg noodles, tagliatelle, or rice.
notes: Fast weeknight dinner; serve with an extra dollop of soured cream if desired[cite: 43].

title: Peppercorn Sauce
keywords: peppercorn sauce, steak sauce, peppercorns, brandy, roux, creamy sauce without cream
instructions: Coarsely crack black peppercorns using a pestle and mortar.
Melt butter in a small saucepan over low heat. Gradually whisk in plain flour to form a smooth paste and cook for 2 minutes.
Add brandy and mix well to cook off the alcohol.
Gradually whisk in milk to form a smooth sauce.
Add chicken stock, cracked peppercorns, and salt.
Simmer gently until sauce reduces to desired consistency.
notes: Cream-free recipe made with a quick roux and milk[cite: 44]. To make ahead, cover surface directly with clingfilm to prevent skin forming[cite: 44].

title: Plum crumble
keywords: plum crumble, victoria plums, cinnamon, ground almonds, demerara, dessert, baking
ingredients: 800g ripe cooking plums (e.g., Victoria), halved and stoned
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C/180°C fan/gas 6.
Place halved plums in a 28cm shallow gratin dish.
Toss light brown sugar, orange zest, cinnamon, and 1 tsp flour together; sprinkle over plums and trickle with 2 tbsp water.
Pulse 250g flour, butter, caster sugar, demerara sugar, and ground almonds in a food processor until mixture just clumps together (or rub butter into flour by hand).
Scatter crumble mixture evenly over plums.
Bake for 30-40 minutes until golden brown. Rest 15 minutes before serving with custard or cream.
notes: Rest for 15 minutes after baking before serving[cite: 45].

title: Pork Chops Baked in Chorizo and Black Olive Tomato Sauce
keywords: pork chops, chorizo, tomato sauce, black olives, spanish, red wine, midweek dinner
ingredients: Rocket leaves and crusty bread (to serve)
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C/160°C fan/gas 4.
Heat oil in a medium saucepan and fry chopped red onion over medium heat for 7-8 minutes until softening.
Add garlic and fry for 1 minute. Stir in chopped chorizo and tomato paste; fry for 3 minutes.
Pour in chopped tomatoes, red wine, and black olives. Bring to a boil, then simmer for 5 minutes.
Transfer sauce into a medium baking dish and bake in the oven for 15 minutes.
Heat a glug of oil in a saucepan over medium-high heat and sear pork chops for 3 minutes per side until browned.
Stir the baked sauce, nestle seared pork chops on top, and bake for a further 15 minutes.
Serve hot with rocket leaves and crusty bread.
notes: Provide crusty bread on the side to soak up the rich, spicy tomato and chorizo sauce[cite: 46].

title: Pork Roast With Crackle
keywords: pork roast, crackling, pork shoulder, boneless, roasted, dinner, cafe delites
ingredients: 4 lb (2 kg) boneless pork shoulder or butt, rind on
instructions: Unwrap pork and lay flat, rind-side up, on a tray. Dry completely in the refrigerator uncovered for at least 1 hour or overnight.
Remove pork from fridge 1-2 hours prior to roasting to reach room temperature.
Preheat oven to 240°C / 460°F.
Score rind with a sharp knife at 1-inch intervals and pat thoroughly dry with paper towels.
Turn skin-side down. Rub garlic powder and 1 tsp salt into the flesh underneath.
Drizzle olive oil over rind and flesh, rubbing in thoroughly. Season rind generously with 1 tbsp sea salt.
Transfer to a roasting dish and roast for 50 minutes until rind begins to crackle.
Reduce temperature to 180°C / 350°F and continue roasting for 1 to 1.5 hours.
Increase temperature back up to 230°C / 440°F and roast for 10 minutes until golden and crisp.
Rest for 15 minutes before carving.
notes: Allowing the skin to dry uncovered in the fridge overnight guarantees perfect, crunchy crackling[cite: 47].

title: ROASTED SKATE
keywords: skate wings, roasted fish, cherry tomatoes, capers, lemon, dijon mustard, quick dinner
ingredients: 2 tbsp extra virgin olive oil (for dressing)
Salt and freshly ground black pepper
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C / gas mark 6.
Toss cherry tomatoes and chilli flakes in 1 tbsp olive oil in a large roasting pan; roast for 10 minutes.
Season skate wings with salt and pepper and place in the roasting pan, shifting tomatoes to one side.
Roast for 15 minutes until fish flesh lifts easily from cartilage.
Whisk extra virgin olive oil, lemon juice, Dijon mustard, and rinsed capers together for dressing.
Pour dressing over fish and tomatoes, returning to oven for 2-3 minutes.
Season to taste and serve immediately with lemon wedges and pan juices.
notes: A simple, healthy seafood meal on the table in under 30 minutes[cite: 48].

title: Salmon and Prawn Tagliatelle
keywords: salmon, prawns, tagliatelle, creme fraiche, pasta, seafood, dill, quick dinner
ingredients: Smoked salmon, cut in bite-size pieces
instructions: Chop onion and fry in olive oil until softened.
Add smoked salmon and sliced mushrooms (if using); warm gently for a few minutes until salmon turns light pink.
Stir in crème fraîche and prawns.
Squeeze 1/2 lemon juice into the sauce and season with black pepper.
Add fresh dill and simmer gently until prawns are fully cooked.
Toss with cooked tagliatelle pasta and top with freshly grated Parmesan cheese.
notes: Takes under 20 minutes from start to finish[cite: 49].

title: Salmon en Croute
keywords: salmon, puff pastry, spinach, cream cheese, chanterelle mushrooms, fine dining, christmas
ingredients: 0.5 tsp black pepper & pinch of salt
instructions: Melt butter in a pan over medium heat; fry mushrooms, shallots, and garlic until softened.
Add fresh spinach, salt, and pepper; cook until spinach wilts.
Stir in cream cheese, breadcrumbs, and dill until mixed, then set aside off heat.
Preheat oven to 180°C / 360°F / gas mark 4 and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Unroll puff pastry onto baking sheet and lay side of salmon in center.
Spread spinach mixture evenly over salmon.
Top with second puff pastry sheet, press down securely, trim excess pastry, and seal edges tightly with a fork.
Score top criss-cross lightly, apply pastry decorations if desired, brush with egg wash, and bake for 30 minutes until golden.
notes: Great impressive center-piece for dinner parties or an alternative Christmas main[cite: 50].

title: Salmon risotto
keywords: salmon, risotto, hot-smoked salmon, white wine, lemon, dill, easy dinner
instructions: Melt butter in a wide shallow pan and cook chopped onion until soft.
Add risotto rice and stir to coat grains.
Pour in white wine and simmer until fully absorbed.
Gradually add warm stock a ladle at a time, stirring constantly until rice is tender.
Stir in lemon juice, lemon zest, flaked hot-smoked salmon, and chopped dill before serving.
notes: Uses hot-smoked salmon flaked in at the end for rich flavor without overcooking[cite: 51].

title: Salted Caramel Peanut Brittle Brownies
keywords: brownies, salted caramel, peanut brittle, dark chocolate, baking, decadent traybake
instructions: To make brittle: boil 150g sugar and water in a pan without stirring until pale cola colored. Remove from heat, sift in bicarb, stir in 150g peanuts, pour onto lined tray, let cool, and crush into pieces.
To make caramel: cook 170g sugar in a pan until melted and pale cola colored. Add cream and sea salt, stirring until smooth and reaches 108°C; set aside to cool.
Preheat oven to 170°C / 150°C fan and line a 33x23cm baking tin.
Melt butter and dark chocolate over a bain-marie; allow to cool slightly.
Whisk eggs, caster sugar, and vanilla together until airy.
Fold melted chocolate into egg mixture, then sift in flour and 1/4 tsp salt.
Pour half brownie batter into tin, layer caramel and crushed brittle/peanuts, then top with remaining batter and gently swirl.
Bake for 35-40 minutes and cool completely in tin.
notes: Combines duplicate recipes (`Salted Caramel Peanut Brittle Brownies.docx` and `.pdf`)[cite: 52, 53].

title: Tasty Sausage Casserole
keywords: sausage casserole, pork sausages, red wine, passata, sun-dried tomatoes, comfort food
ingredients: 8 good quality pork sausages, cut into bite-sized pieces
instructions: Fry sliced sausages in olive oil in a large pan until golden and cooked through; remove and set aside.
In the same pan, fry onions and garlic for 5 minutes until softened.
Add chopped pepper, mushrooms, and sun-dried tomatoes; cook for a few minutes before returning sausages to pan.
Turn heat to high, pour in red wine, and reduce slightly for 2-3 minutes.
Add passata, sugar, paprika, and basil. Simmer gently for 30 minutes.
Season to taste and serve with rice, crusty bread, or pasta.
notes: Flavors deepen when made in advance and reheated the next day[cite: 54].

title: Sausage, sage & onion stuffing
keywords: stuffing, cumberland sausages, sage, onion, bramley apple, granary breadcrumbs, christmas
ingredients: 1 small Bramley apple, peeled, cored, and diced
2 x 400g packs meaty Cumberland sausages (skins removed)
Handful fresh sage, leaves chopped (plus extra for garnish)
instructions: Fry sliced onions in butter for 5 minutes until soft.
Add diced Bramley apple, cook briefly, and remove from heat to cool.
Mix cooled onion mixture with sausage meat, chopped sage, and granary breadcrumbs; season well.
Use to stuff poultry or roll into balls/pack into a 1kg loaf tin topped with extra sage leaves.
Bake in oven at 190°C/170°C fan for 30-40 minutes until cooked through.
notes: Pairs perfectly with roast turkey or chicken[cite: 55].

title: Sausages with sticky onion gravy
keywords: sausages, sticky onions, beef stock, gravy, worcestershire sauce, thyme, quick dinner
ingredients: 1 batch Basic sticky onions (50g butter, 12 medium onions, 1 tsp sugar)
instructions: For the onions: Melt 50g butter in a large deep frying pan, stir through 12 sliced medium onions, cover, and cook gently for 10 minutes until softened[cite: 56]. Remove lid, add 1 tsp sugar, and cook for 15-20 minutes, stirring, until liquid evaporates and onions turn golden[cite: 56]. Divide into 3 batches[cite: 56].
Fry sausages for 15 minutes or until browned, then remove from pan and keep warm[cite: 56].
Heat 1 batch of basic sticky onions in the same pan, then add plain flour, stirring for 1 minute[cite: 56].
Add picked thyme leaves, then gradually stir in beef stock[cite: 56].
Bring to a boil, then simmer for 5 minutes until smooth[cite: 56].
Add a splash of Worcestershire sauce, season to taste, and serve poured over the warm sausages[cite: 56].
notes: Basic sticky onions recipe makes 3 batches; remaining batches can be kept in the fridge for up to 5 days or frozen for 1 month[cite: 56].

title: Slow Cooker Beef Brisket with BBQ Sauce
keywords: beef brisket, slow cooker, bbq sauce, american, southern, roasted, dinner, recipetineats
ingredients: 1/2 cup / 110g brown sugar, packed (for BBQ sauce)
2 tsp EACH black pepper, onion powder, mustard powder (for BBQ sauce)
instructions: Mix rub ingredients together in a bowl and rub all over brisket[cite: 57].
Combine all BBQ sauce ingredients in a slow cooker and submerge the brisket[cite: 57].
Slow cook on low for 8 hours (1.5 kg) to 10 hours (2 kg)[cite: 57].
Remove brisket onto a baking tray[cite: 57]. Pour remaining slow cooker liquid into a saucepan and simmer over medium-high heat until reduced to a syrup consistency[cite: 57].
Drizzle brisket with oil and roast at 200°C / 390°F for 15 minutes until browned spots appear[cite: 57].
Baste generously with reduced BBQ sauce and return to oven for 5 minutes; repeat basting and roasting for 5-10 minutes until deeply caramelised[cite: 57].
Slice thinly across the grain and serve with remaining sauce[cite: 57].
notes: Can also be cooked in a pressure cooker (1 hr 15 mins to 1 hr 30 mins) or oven (4 hours covered at 160°C)[cite: 57].

title: Slow Cooker Chicken Curry
keywords: chicken curry, slow cooker, indian, chicken thighs, potatoes, gluten free, kid friendly
ingredients: 8 boneless skinless chicken thighs, cut into 1-inch pieces
instructions: Heat oil in a pan and sauté chopped onions and minced garlic for 3-4 minutes until softened[cite: 58].

Transfer sautéed mixture to slow cooker along with baby potatoes, chicken thigh pieces, bay leaf, cloves, peppercorns, green chilli, all spices, salt, tomato puree, water, and butter; mix well[cite: 58].
Cover and cook on high for 3.5-4 hours (or on low for 6 hours)[cite: 58].
Stir in freshly chopped coriander and serve hot over steamed rice or with butter naan[cite: 58].
notes: Chicken thighs are recommended as they stay juicy in the slow cooker without drying out[cite: 58].

title: Smoked Chipotle Chicken
keywords: smoked chicken, chipotle, bbq, smoker, paprika, cumin, spice rub
instructions: Combine chipotle powder, smoked paprika, garlic powder, cumin, coriander, salt, and brown sugar in a bowl to make the dry rub[cite: 59].
Apply rub evenly over the chicken flesh and skin[cite: 59].
Preheat smoker to 120°C - 130°C[cite: 59].
Smoke chicken for between 3 and 5 hours until a probe thermometer inserted into the thickest part of the thigh reads 74°C[cite: 59].
notes: Ensure internal temperature reaches 74°C in the thickest part of the thigh for safe consumption[cite: 59].

title: Smoky Hake, Beans & Greens
keywords: hake, chorizo, spinach, cannellini beans, seafood, smoked paprika, healthy, fast dinner
ingredients: 100g raw cooking chorizo, squeezed from casing
instructions: Heat 1 tsp oil in a large frying pan, squeeze chorizo meat into pan, add chopped onion, and fry for 5 minutes, breaking up chorizo with a spatula until golden[cite: 60].
Wilt spinach by pouring boiling water over it in a colander, refresh under cold water, squeeze dry with hands, and set aside[cite: 60].
Place hake fillets on a foil-lined, oiled baking tray, season with salt, pepper, smoked paprika, and a drizzle of oil[cite: 60]. Grill on high for 5 minutes until flaky[cite: 60].
Add shredded chilli to chorizo pan and fry for 1 minute, then stir in cannellini beans, wilted spinach, lemon juice, and extra virgin olive oil to warm through gently[cite: 60].
Spoon bean and spinach mixture onto plates and top with grilled hake fillets[cite: 60].
notes: Optionally serve with quick garlic mayonnaise on the side[cite: 60].

title: Classic White Sourdough Bread
keywords: sourdough bread, sourdough starter, artisan bread, baking, homemade bread, levain
instructions: Mix salt through flour in a clean bowl, then add water and active sourdough starter to form a rough dough[cite: 61].
Turn dough out onto a clean work surface and knead for approximately 10 minutes until smooth, soft, and elastic (windowpane test)[cite: 61].
Return to bowl, cover, and allow to prove for 4 hours at room temperature[cite: 61].
Knock back dough, form into a tight round ball, and place seam-side up into a floured proving basket (or floured tea-towel-lined Pyrex dish)[cite: 61].
Cover and prove for another 3–3.5 hours at room temperature, or overnight in the fridge[cite: 61].
Preheat oven to 230°C / 210°C fan with a shallow tray in the bottom[cite: 61].

Turn loaf out onto a tray, score top with a sharp knife 1/2 cm deep, pour boiling water into bottom tray to create steam, and bake for 30–35 minutes until golden and hollow sounding when tapped[cite: 61].
notes: Includes full 7-day starter creation guide and Pyrex dish baking alternative[cite: 61].

title: Flavoured Sourdough Bread

baseInstructions: Pour the water into a mixing bowl or large container, add the sourdough starter, and stir to break up and distribute the starter[cite: 12].
Add the flour gradually, mixing until a rough dough has formed[cite: 12].
Cover and leave for 30 minutes to 1 hour[cite: 12].
Perform stretch and folds 6 times at 30-minute intervals[cite: 12].
Leave to rise until doubled in size[cite: 12].
Turn out onto a work surface, stretch into a rectangle, and perform a letter fold from top to bottom and bottom to top, then repeat for the sides[cite: 12].
Form a round by dragging the dough towards you across the surface while tucking your fingers under the bottom, turn through 90 degrees, and repeat until smooth and tight[cite: 12].
Leave to bench rest for 15 minutes, shaping and resting again if necessary[cite: 12].
Flour a banneton or a tea towel in a bowl and turn the dough into it seam side up[cite: 12].
Leave to rise overnight in the fridge or for a few hours on the work surface, using the poke test to determine readiness[cite: 12].
Heat the oven to 230°C / 210°C fan with a roasting tin in the bottom[cite: 12].
Scatter flour over the dough, turn out onto a tray, cut a pattern into the top, and bake for 35 minutes while adding 200ml of water into the roasting tin[cite: 12].

title: Sourdough Hot Cross Buns
keywords: hot cross buns, sourdough, easter, mixed spice, sultanas, mixed peel, glazed buns
instructions: Mix bread flour, spices, sugar, and salt in a bowl[cite: 63]. Rub in butter with fingertips, then stir in sultanas and mixed peel[cite: 63].
Make a well in center, add egg, sourdough starter, and warm water[cite: 63]. Mix into a soft dough and knead until smooth and elastic[cite: 63].
Place in oiled bowl, cover, and rise in a warm place for 12 hours[cite: 63].
Knead gently, divide into 12 balls, place 2cm apart on greased tray, cover, and rise for 10-12 hours until doubled[cite: 63].
Preheat oven to 190°C / 180°C fan[cite: 63]. Mix plain flour with cold water to a soft paste and pipe crosses over buns[cite: 63].
Bake for 20-25 minutes until golden[cite: 63]. Heat glaze ingredients (sugar, water, spice) until dissolved and brush over warm buns[cite: 63].

title: Sourdough Pancakes
keywords: sourdough pancakes, starter discard, breakfast, einkorn flour, fast pancakes, fluffy
instructions: Melt butter in a large bowl and allow to cool slightly[cite: 64]. Whisk in eggs, milk, and vanilla extract[cite: 64].
Stir in sourdough starter until incorporated[cite: 64].
Add flour, baking soda, baking powder, and salt; stir well[cite: 64]. Let batter rest for 30 minutes[cite: 64].
Preheat griddle or skillet[cite: 64].
Ladle 1/3 cup of batter onto hot griddle per pancake[cite: 64]. Cook 2-3 minutes until bubbles form on top and edges set, then flip and cook 1-2 minutes more[cite: 64].
Serve hot with butter and pure maple syrup[cite: 64].
notes: Excellent recipe for utilizing leftover sourdough starter discard[cite: 64].

title: Authentic Sourdough Pizza
keywords: sourdough pizza, pizza dough, levain, ooni, italian, 00 flour, long ferment
instructions: Build Levain: Mix 50g starter, 50g 00 flour, 50g whole grain flour, and 100g warm water in a jar[cite: 65]. Cover and let double (3-4 hours)[cite: 65].

Final Mix: Dissolve 10g salt in 310g warm water in a bowl[cite: 65]. Stir in 200g levain mix[cite: 65]. Slowly mix in 425g 00 flour and 75g whole grain flour by hand[cite: 65]. Rest 10 minutes[cite: 65].
Knead 10-15 minutes by hand until smooth, bouncy, and elastic[cite: 65]. Tighten into a round[cite: 65].
Bulk Ferment: Place dough in an oiled container, cover, and let double at room temperature for 3 hours[cite: 65].
Divide & Ball: Divide into 3-4 equal pieces, ball up tightly, place on floured tray, cover, and cold prove in fridge for 24 hours[cite: 65].
Bring dough balls to room temperature for 2 hours before stretching[cite: 65].
Stretch dough to 12 inches on a floured peel, top as desired, and bake in a high-temperature pizza oven (500°C / 932°F) until charred and crisp[cite: 65].
notes: Requires starting the levain processing the morning of the day before cooking[cite: 65].

title: Spanish Stuffed Marrow
keywords: marrow, chorizo, manchego, tomatoes, roasted red peppers, breadcrumbs, spanish
ingredients: 140g roasted red pepper from a jar, sliced
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C / 180°C fan / gas mark 6[cite: 66].
Cut the marrow in half lengthways, scoop out the central seeds/pith, place cut-side up in a large roasting tin, and season[cite: 66].
Heat olive oil in a saucepan and sweat diced onion over low heat for 10 minutes until soft[cite: 66].
Add garlic, chopped chorizo, smoked paprika, cayenne pepper, oregano, and thyme; cook for a few minutes[cite: 66].
Add chopped tomatoes and sliced roasted red peppers, lower heat to a simmer, and cook for 10 minutes before stirring through chopped parsley[cite: 66].
Spoon tomato and chorizo mixture into marrow halves, cover with foil, and bake for 30 minutes[cite: 66].
Remove foil, sprinkle over breadcrumbs and grated Manchego, and bake uncovered for a further 10 minutes until golden and marrow is tender[cite: 66].
notes: A great way to use up large seasonal garden marrows[cite: 66].

title: Glazed Sprouts with Caramelised Red Onions
keywords: brussels sprouts, red onions, demerara sugar, sherry vinegar, christmas sides, vegetable side
instructions: Melt butter in a large heavy-based frying pan over medium heat, add red onion wedges, and cook for 6-8 minutes until golden and caramelised[cite: 67].
Meanwhile, cook Brussels sprouts in a pan of boiling salted water for 3-4 minutes until just tender[cite: 67].
Stir demerara sugar and sherry vinegar into the onions and allow to bubble for a few seconds[cite: 67].
Remove onions from heat, drain sprouts thoroughly, and toss sprouts through the caramelised onion mixture[cite: 67].
notes: Excellent vibrant festive accompaniment for Christmas or Sunday roasts[cite: 67].

title: 10 Quick & Easy Steak Sauces
keywords: steak sauces, salsa verde, peppercorn sauce, bearnaise, chimichurri, black bean, red wine jus, teriyaki, blue cheese, mushroom sauce
ingredients: Salsa Verde: Parsley, chives, mint, 1 tsp capers, 2-3 anchovies, 1 garlic clove, 1 lemon, 3 tbsp olive oil[cite: 68].
Smart Peppercorn: 2 tbsp white wine vinegar, 150ml chicken stock, 2 tsp green peppercorns, 4 tbsp double cream[cite: 68].
Cheat's Béarnaise: 25g butter, 1 shallot, 1 tsp white wine vinegar, 100g crème fraîche, 1 tsp Dijon mustard, 1/2 tsp capers, chopped tarragon[cite: 68].
Spicy Chimichurri: 1 garlic clove, 1 red chilli, coriander, parsley, 3 tbsp red wine vinegar, 2 tbsp olive oil[cite: 68].

Black Bean & Sesame: 1/2 can black beans, 1 tsp dark brown sugar, 2 tsp honey, 1 tsp five-spice, 1/2 tsp ginger, 1 red chilli, 2 tsp tahini, 2 tbsp cider vinegar, 2 tsp soy sauce, 5 tbsp water[cite: 68].
Quick Red Wine: 250ml beef stock, 125ml red wine, 2 tsp dark brown sugar, 1 tsp balsamic vinegar[cite: 68].

instructions: Salsa Verde (15m): Chop herbs, capers, anchovies, garlic; whisk with lemon juice and olive oil[cite: 68].
Smart Peppercorn (20m): Simmer vinegar, reduce chicken stock by half, crush in green peppercorns, and thicken with double cream[cite: 68].

Black Bean & Sesame (20m): Blend black beans, spices, tahini, vinegar, soy sauce, and water; simmer for 5 mins[cite: 68].
Quick Red Wine (25m): Reduce beef stock by half, add red wine, sugar, and balsamic vinegar; reduce again until glossy[cite: 68].
Teriyaki (20m): Simmer soy sauce, sake, mirin, ginger, and honey for 5 mins; stir in sliced spring onions[cite: 68].

Blue Cheese (20m): Make a roux with butter, flour, and milk; stir in Stilton until melted and smooth[cite: 68].
Mushroom (15m): Fry sliced mushrooms in oil, add garlic and brandy (evaporate), then stir in double cream and wholegrain mustard[cite: 68].
notes: Includes 10 speedy steak sauce choices created by the BBC Good Food cookery team[cite: 68].

title: Tandoori Dry Rub
keywords: tandoori, spice blend, dry rub, indian, barbecue, chicken rub, seasoning
instructions: Measure all ground spices, salt, and garlic powder into a bowl or jar[cite: 69].
Whisk or shake thoroughly to blend evenly[cite: 69].
Store in an airtight spice container and use as a dry rub for chicken, meats, or grilled vegetables[cite: 69].
notes: Yields approximately 1/3 cup of aromatic spice blend[cite: 69].

title: Thai Butternut Squash Soup
keywords: thai soup, butternut squash, red curry paste, coconut milk, lemongrass, galangal, spicy soup
ingredients: Curry Paste: 1 shallot, 1 stalk lemongrass, 1-2 red chillies, 4 garlic cloves, 1 thumb galangal/ginger, 2 tbsp tomato ketchup, 1 tsp cumin, 3/4 tsp coriander, 1/4 tsp white pepper, 2 tbsp fish sauce (or soy), 1 tsp shrimp paste, 1 tsp sugar, 1.5-2 tbsp chilli powder, 3 tbsp coconut milk, 2 tbsp lime juice[cite: 70].

Soup Base: 1 tbsp olive oil, 1 onion (chopped), 2 tsp minced fresh ginger, 1 tbsp Thai red curry paste, 2 lb butternut squash (cubed), 450ml vegetable stock, 1 can (13.5 oz) light coconut milk, salt and pepper[cite: 70].
instructions: Blitz all homemade Thai curry paste ingredients in a blender until smooth[cite: 70].
Heat 1 tbsp olive oil in a large pot over medium heat[cite: 70]. Add chopped onion and stir for 1 minute, then add ginger and 1 tbsp curry paste; stir 1 minute more[cite: 70].
Add cubed butternut squash and vegetable stock[cite: 70].
Bring to a boil, then simmer over low heat for 15-20 minutes until squash is tender[cite: 70].
Cool slightly, purée with an immersion blender until smooth, return to heat, stir in light coconut milk, season, and warm through[cite: 70].

title: The Best Spaghetti Bolognese
keywords: spaghetti bolognese, beef mince, bacon, red wine, parmesan, Italian, pasta, classic
ingredients: 4 rashers smoked streaky bacon, finely chopped
Small pack basil leaves (3/4 chopped, 1/4 whole for garnish)
1 red chilli, deseeded and finely chopped (optional)
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large saucepan, add chopped bacon, and fry for 10 minutes until golden[cite: 71].
Reduce heat, add onions, carrots, celery, garlic, and chopped rosemary leaves; fry for 10 minutes until softened[cite: 71].
Increase heat, add beef mince, and cook for 3-4 minutes until browned[cite: 71].
Add plum tomatoes, chopped basil, oregano, bay leaves, tomato purée, beef stock cube, red chilli, red wine, and halved cherry tomatoes; break up plum tomatoes with a spoon[cite: 71].
Bring to a boil, reduce to a gentle simmer, cover, and cook for 1 hour 15 minutes[cite: 71].
Stir in grated parmesan and check seasoning[cite: 71].
Cook spaghetti according to pack instructions, drain, and serve tossed with sauce, fresh basil leaves, extra parmesan, and crusty bread[cite: 71].
notes: Simmering gently for over an hour creates a rich, thick, deeply flavored meat sauce[cite: 71].

title: Tita Em's Chicken Wings Adobo
keywords: chicken wings, adobo, filipino, soy sauce, rice vinegar, coconut milk, garlic, kuma inn
ingredients: 2.5 lb chicken wings, tips removed and sectioned
instructions: Combine rice vinegar, soy sauce, crushed garlic, peppercorns, bay leaves, and 1 1/4 cups water in a large saucepan[cite: 72]. Add chicken wings and marinate at room temperature for 30 minutes[cite: 72].
Cover saucepan, bring to a boil over high heat, reduce heat to low, and simmer covered for 30-40 minutes until tender[cite: 72].
Remove chicken wings from liquid and drain on a wire rack[cite: 72].
Heat vegetable oil in a skillet and fry wings until golden brown[cite: 72].
Boil braising liquid, stir in coconut milk, and bring to a simmer[cite: 72]. Toss fried wings back into sauce to coat and serve[cite: 72].
notes: Signature recipe from Kuma Inn NYC inspired by Filipino adobo[cite: 72].

title: Weeknight Porchetta
keywords: porchetta, pork tenderloin, bacon, fennel seeds, rosemary, quick roast, alison roman
ingredients: 4 garlic cloves, finely chopped (plus 2 whole heads, halved crosswise)
instructions: Preheat oven to 425°F (220°C)[cite: 73].
Mix chopped garlic, chopped rosemary, fennel seeds, salt, 1 tbsp olive oil, and black pepper in a bowl[cite: 73]. Rub mixture all over pork tenderloin[cite: 73].
Scatter rosemary sprigs in a baking dish and place tenderloin on top[cite: 73].
Wrap bacon slices around tenderloin, tucking ends underneath to hold in place[cite: 73].
Nestle halved heads of garlic around tenderloin and drizzle remaining 1 tbsp olive oil over garlic and meat[cite: 73].
Roast for 30-40 minutes until meat thermometer registers 145°F (63°C)[cite: 73]. Rest 10 minutes before slicing[cite: 73].
notes: A fast weeknight version of classic Italian porchetta using pork tenderloin and bacon[cite: 73].

title: White Chocolate & Ginger Cheesecake with Ginger Butterscotch Sauce
keywords: cheesecake, white chocolate, ginger, gingernut biscuits, butterscotch sauce, mascarpone, dessert
instructions: Line a 20cm cake tin with greaseproof paper strip and a double layer of cling film[cite: 74].
Crush gingernut biscuits to fine crumbs and mix with 100g melted butter[cite: 74]. Press firmly into tin and chill in fridge for 30 minutes[cite: 74].
Mix cream cheese, mascarpone, and 150ml double cream until smooth[cite: 74]. Whisk in 400g melted white chocolate[cite: 74]. Pour over base and chill for several hours or overnight[cite: 74].
To make sauce: heat sugar in a pan until golden caramel forms[cite: 74]. Off heat, swirl in butter, whisk in 120ml double cream, then stir in chopped stem ginger and ginger syrup[cite: 74].
Drizzle warm or cooled ginger butterscotch sauce over sliced cheesecake before serving[cite: 74].

title: Best Yorkshire Puddings
keywords: yorkshire puddings, sunday roast, British, batter, roasted, sides
ingredients: Pinch of salt and black pepper
instructions: Preheat oven to 230°C / 210°C fan / gas mark 8[cite: 75]. Drizzle sunflower oil evenly into a 12-hole muffin tin or 2 x 4-hole Yorkshire pudding tins and place in oven to get smoking hot[cite: 75].
Whisk flour and eggs in a bowl until smooth[cite: 75].
Gradually add milk, beating continuously until batter is lump-free[cite: 75]. Season with salt and pepper and transfer into a pouring jug[cite: 75].
Carefully pour batter into hot tins and return immediately to oven[cite: 75].

title: Honey-Garlic Pork Tenderloin
keywords: pork tenderloin, honey garlic, glaze, grilled pork, oven roasted pork, barbecue, quick dinner
ingredients: 2 whole pork tenderloins (approx. 1.5 to 2 lbs total)
instructions: Whisk honey, minced garlic, soy sauce, apple cider vinegar, and Dijon mustard together; divide in half (one for raw meat, one for serving)[cite: 76].
Trim silver skin from pork, pat dry, tuck thin tail ends under by 2 inches, tie with butcher's twine, rub with oil, and season with salt, pepper, and garlic powder[cite: 76].

Grill method: Sear on direct heat at 400°F (200°C) for 2-3 mins per side, move to indirect heat, brush with glaze, and cook lid-closed for 12-15 mins until internal temp reaches 145°F (63°C)[cite: 76].
Oven method: Sear in a hot skillet for 2 mins per side, brush with glaze, transfer to a 400°F (200°C) oven, and roast for 13-15 mins until 145°F (63°C)[cite: 76].

title: Sous Vide Steak
keywords: sous vide, steak, temperature chart, ribeye, strip steak, tenderloin, searing
