ingredients: 1.5-inch to 2-inch thick steaks (Ribeye, New York Strip, Porterhouse, or Tenderloin)
Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
Optional aromatics: fresh thyme or rosemary sprigs, garlic cloves
High-smoke-point oil (neutral oil, vegetable oil, or clarified butter) for searing
instructions: Preheat sous vide precision cooker to target temperature according to preferred doneness chart.
Season steak generously with salt and pepper. Place in vacuum-seal or heavy-duty Ziploc bag along with optional herb sprigs.
Seal bag (using vacuum sealer or water displacement method) and submerge in water bath for recommended time.
Remove steak from bag and pat completely dry on all sides using paper towels.
Heat heavy cast-iron or stainless-steel skillet over high heat with 1 tbsp neutral oil until smoking.
Sear steak rapidly for 30 to 45 seconds per side until a deep brown crust forms, turning frequently.
Serve immediately (no resting required after sous vide searing).
notes: Food Safety Note: Do not cook steaks below 130°F (54°C) for longer than 2.5 hours.

title: Thai red chicken curry

curry: 4 heaped tbsp homemade Thai red curry paste
6 baby aubergines or 1 aubergine, cut into chunks
Handful of fresh Thai basil or fresh coriander, chopped
thai_red_curry_paste: 2 dried red chillies, soaked in hot water for 10 minutes
3 lemongrass stalks, outer skin removed, finely sliced
4 coriander roots roughly chopped (or stalks from a large bunch of fresh coriander)
6 fresh kaffir lime leaves or finely grated zest of 1 lime
5cm piece fresh galangal or ginger, finely grated

instructions: To make the paste, process or pound the ingredients starting with dry spices, aromatics, and finally puréed chillies until a paste forms.
To make the curry, heat the oil in a wok or frying pan and fry the shallots for 5 minutes until softened.
Add the garlic and fry for 30 seconds more.
Stir in the Thai red curry paste, fish sauce, palm sugar, kaffir lime leaves, and coconut milk, then bring to a gentle simmer.
Add the aubergine chunks and simmer until slightly softened.
Add the sliced chicken and cook for another 10 minutes.
Add the green beans and cook for a further 5 minutes until tender.
Remove from the heat, taste and adjust with more fish sauce if needed.
Stir in the herbs and serve immediately with steamed or coconut rice and lime wedges.

title: Beer Gravy

main: Pan drippings (from roasted turkey or chicken)
1 bottle (12 oz) beer (preferably an amber ale, brown ale, or porter)
Salt and freshly cracked black pepper, to taste

instructions: Pour pan drippings into a fat separator or glass measuring cup, letting the fat rise to the top. Reserve both the fat and the rich liquid underneath.
In a saucepan over medium heat, melt 3 tablespoons of fat (or butter).
Whisk in the flour and cook for 1 to 2 minutes until bubbly and light brown to form a roux.
Slowly pour in the beer while whisking continuously to prevent lumps.
Gradually whisk in the reserved pan drippings and stock until desired consistency is reached.
Simmer for 5 to 10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until thickened.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste and serve warm.

title: Pork chops baked in chorizo and black olive tomato sauce

main: 100g cooking chorizo, skin removed and diced
Handful of fresh flat-leaf parsley, chopped
Crusty bread or mashed potatoes, to serve

instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C/160°C fan/gas 4.
Heat the olive oil in a large, ovenproof skillet or casserole dish over high heat.
Season the pork chops and sear for 2 minutes on each side until browned, then remove and set aside on a plate.
Turn down the heat to medium, add the diced chorizo and onion to the pan, and fry for 5 minutes until the onion is soft and the chorizo has released its oil.
Stir in the garlic and smoked paprika, frying for another minute until fragrant.
Pour in the canned tomatoes and chicken stock, then bring to a simmer.
Return the pork chops (and any resting juices) to the pan, along with the black olives, nestling them into the sauce.
Transfer to the oven and bake uncovered for 20-25 minutes until the pork is cooked through and tender.
Scatter over the fresh chopped parsley and serve hot with crusty bread or mashed potatoes.

title: Paprika Pork
keywords: paprika, pork, bbc good food, stew, easy dinner, quick meal
ingredients: 500g pork tenderloin, cut into bite-sized pieces
Rice or crusty bread, to serve
instructions: Heat the oil in a large skillet or casserole dish over medium-high heat.
Add the onion and fry for 3–4 minutes until soft.
Stir in the smoked paprika and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the pork tenderloin pieces and cook for 3–5 minutes until browned all over.
Add the sliced red and yellow peppers along with the button mushrooms.
Pour in the chicken stock and bring to a simmer. Cover and cook over medium heat for 10–12 minutes until the pork is cooked through and tender.
Remove from the heat and stir through the reduced-fat sour cream and fresh parsley.
Serve warm over rice or with crusty bread.
notes: Ensure the heat is low or turned off before stirring in sour cream to prevent curdling.

title: Sam's Toad in the Hole
keywords: toad in the hole, sausages, yorkshire pudding, comfort food, British, classic
instructions: Heat the oven to 220°C/200°C fan/gas 7.
Whisk the flour, eggs, and milk together with a pinch of salt until smooth to create the batter. Let sit for 10-15 minutes.
Put 2 tbsp of oil or lard into a metal baking tin or roasting dish (approx 20x30cm) and add the sausages.
Place in the oven for 10-15 minutes until the sausages are sizzling and starting to brown.
Carefully take the dish out of the oven and quickly pour the batter over the hot oil and sausages.
Return immediately to the oven and bake for 25-30 minutes, without opening the oven door, until the batter is dramatically risen, golden, and crisp.
Serve hot immediately with rich onion gravy.
notes: Resist opening the oven door during the first 25 minutes of baking to prevent the batter from deflating.

title: Felicity Cloake's Perfect Jerk Chicken
keywords: jerk chicken, barbecue, Jamaican, scotch bonnet, spicy, marinade, Felicity Cloake
ingredients: 1 tbsp dried thyme (or 2 tbsp fresh thyme leaves)
3-4 Scotch Bonnet chillies, deseeded and chopped
thumb-sized piece fresh ginger, peeled and chopped
instructions: In a dry skillet, toast the allspice berries and peppercorns for 1–2 minutes until fragrant. Grind to a powder in a spice grinder or mortar.
Place ground spices into a food processor with thyme, salt, nutmeg, cinnamon, Scotch Bonnets, garlic, ginger, spring onions, sugar, soy sauce, lime juice, rum, and vegetable oil.
Blend to a thick paste.
Slash each piece of chicken 2–3 times down to the bone.
Coat the chicken pieces thoroughly with the jerk paste, rubbing it into the slashes. Cover and refrigerate for at least 12 hours (preferably 24 hours).
Prepare a barbecue for indirect medium-heat cooking, adding soaked pimento/allspice wood chips if available.
Place chicken on the cooler side of the grill, cover, and cook for 35-40 minutes, turning occasionally.
Finish by moving chicken directly over the coals for 5 minutes to char the skin.
Ensure meat reaches internal temp of 75°C (165°F). Serve with rice and peas.
notes: Wear gloves when handling Scotch Bonnet chillies to prevent skin irritation.

title: Traditional South African Biltong
keywords: biltong, cured beef, South African, jerky, coriander, vinegar, dried meat
ingredients: 100ml brown spirit vinegar or apple cider vinegar
Biltong box or well-ventilated drying area
instructions: Slice the beef along the grain into long strips about 1 inch (2.5 cm) thick.
Toast coriander seeds in a dry pan until aromatic, then coarsely crush in a mortar or grinder.
Mix crushed coriander, coarse salt, brown sugar, black pepper, and optional cayenne pepper together in a bowl.
Splash vinegar over meat strips, ensuring all sides are coated.
Dredge the meat through the spice mixture, coating evenly.
Layer meat in a glass or food-safe plastic container, cover, and refrigerate for 12 to 24 hours (turning once).
Remove meat from container, wipe off excess liquid and heavy clumps of salt.
Insert biltong hooks or thread string through the thick end of each strip.
Hang strips in a cool, dark, dry area with good airflow (or a dedicated biltong box) for 3 to 5 days depending on preferred dryness.
Slice thinly across the grain to serve.
notes: Ensure high airflow and low humidity during curing to prevent mold.

title: Classic South African Bobotie
keywords: bobotie, South African, spiced minced meat, custard topping, curry, chutney
ingredients: 1kg lean minced beef (or mixture of beef and lamb)
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C/160°C fan/gas 4.
Soak bread in 100ml of milk, then squeeze excess milk back into bowl and mash bread with a fork.
Heat oil in a large skillet and fry chopped onions for 5 minutes until soft.
Add garlic and minced beef, frying until browned.
Stir in curry powder, cumin, turmeric, cinnamon, dried herbs, sultanas, mashed soaked bread, mango chutney, and lemon juice. Season with salt and pepper.
Spoon meat mixture into an ovenproof casserole dish and press down evenly.
Press bay leaves into the top of the meat.
Whisk remaining milk (275ml) with 2 eggs and season lightly.
Pour egg mixture evenly over meat dish.
Bake for 35-40 minutes until egg topping is golden and set. Serve with yellow rice.
notes: Serve traditionally with yellow turmeric rice and sambal side dishes.

title: Kerala Egg Puffs
keywords: egg puffs, Kerala style, bakery style, puff pastry, spiced egg, Indian snack
ingredients: 6 hard-boiled eggs, peeled and halved lengthwise
2 tbsp coconut oil or vegetable oil
instructions: Heat oil in a pan, add curry leaves, green chillies, and sliced onions. Sauté until translucent and lightly browned.
Add ginger-garlic paste and sauté until raw smell disappears.
Add turmeric, chilli powder, coriander powder, garam masala, and salt. Cook on low heat for 2 minutes until oil separates.
Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Roll out puff pastry sheet and cut into 6 equal rectangles.
Place a spoon of onion masala mixture in the center of each pastry square.
Place half a boiled egg cut-side down on top of the masala.
Fold opposite corners of pastry over egg, sealing edges with water.
Brush tops with beaten egg wash.
Bake for 20-25 minutes until puff pastry is puffed and golden brown.
notes: Press edges down firmly to ensure the pastry doesn't unfold during baking.

title: Copycat Chipotle Barbacoa Beef
keywords: barbacoa, chipotle copycat, shredded beef, Mexican, tacos, burritos, slow cooker
ingredients: 1.5kg (3 lbs) beef chuck roast, cut into large chunks
3-4 chipotle peppers in adobo sauce, plus 2 tbsp adobo sauce
instructions: In a blender, combine chipotle peppers, adobo sauce, garlic, beef broth, lime juice, apple cider vinegar, oregano, cumin, ground cloves, salt, and pepper. Blend until smooth.
Heat vegetable oil in a large skillet over high heat. Sear beef chunks on all sides until deeply browned.
Transfer seared beef to slow cooker.
Pour blended adobo sauce over beef and add bay leaves.
Cover and cook on LOW for 8-9 hours (or HIGH for 4-5 hours) until meat easily shreds with two forks.
Remove bay leaves. Shred beef inside slow cooker and let it absorb juices for 10 minutes before serving in burritos or tacos.
notes: Can also be cooked in an Instant Pot on High Pressure for 60 minutes with a 15-minute natural release.

title: Thai Red Curry with Chicken
keywords: thai red curry, chicken curry, coconut milk, authentic thai, quick dinner
ingredients: 1 cup bamboo shoots or snow peas
1 tbsp palm sugar or brown sugar
instructions: Heat oil in a large skillet or wok over medium-high heat.
Add red curry paste, garlic, ginger, and lemongrass. Fry for 1–2 minutes until fragrant.
Add ½ cup of coconut milk and stir constantly until oil starts separating from paste.
Add sliced chicken and toss to coat in paste for 2 minutes.
Pour in remaining coconut milk and chicken stock. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Add bell pepper and bamboo shoots. Simmer for 5–7 minutes until chicken is cooked through.
Stir in fish sauce, sugar, and lime juice. Turn off heat.
Stir through Thai basil leaves and serve immediately over hot Jasmine rice.
notes: Full-fat coconut milk provides the best creaminess and richness for authentic texture.

title: Butternut Squash Chicken Street Tacos
keywords: tacos, street tacos, butternut squash, chicken, roasted, Mexican, quick dinner
ingredients: 2 cups butternut squash, peeled and cubed (½-inch)
½ cup crumbled feta or cotija cheese
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F).
Toss cubed butternut squash with 1 tbsp olive oil, chili powder, cumin, salt, and pepper.
Spread squash evenly on a baking sheet and roast for 20 minutes until tender and caramelized.
Heat remaining 1 tbsp olive oil in a skillet over medium heat.
Add diced chicken and taco seasoning. Cook for 6-8 minutes until chicken is browned and cooked through.
Warm corn tortillas in a dry skillet or directly over gas burner flame for 10-15 seconds per side.
Assemble tacos by placing roasted squash and chicken onto warmed tortillas.
Garnish with crumbled cotija cheese, fresh cilantro, and a squeeze of lime juice.
notes: Double up corn tortillas per taco if serving street-style to prevent tearing.

title: Crème Brûlée Cheesecake Bars
keywords: creme brulee, cheesecake, bars, dessert, graham cracker, caramelized sugar
ingredients: ¼ cup granulated sugar or superfine sugar (for torching/topping)
instructions: Preheat oven to 160°C (325°F) and line an 8x8-inch baking pan with parchment paper.
Combine graham cracker crumbs, melted butter, and 2 tbsp sugar in a bowl. Press firmly into the bottom of the prepared pan.
In a large bowl, beat the softened cream cheese and ½ cup sugar until smooth and creamy.
Add eggs one at a time, beating well after each addition. Stir in vanilla extract and heavy cream until just combined.
Pour the cheesecake filling over the crust and smooth the top.
Bake for 35–40 minutes until the edges are set but the center still has a slight wobble.
Remove from oven and allow to cool completely at room temperature, then refrigerate for at least 4 hours (or overnight).
Once chilled, cut into square bars.
Sprinkle a thin, even layer of sugar over the top of each bar and caramelize using a kitchen blowtorch until golden and crispy.
notes: If you don't have a kitchen torch, you can brown the sugar layer under a hot oven broiler for 1–2 minutes, watching closely.

title: Rhubarb Crumble Cheesecake
keywords: rhubarb, crumble, cheesecake, Jane's Patisserie, baking, no-bake, dessert
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C/160°C fan/gas 4.
Toss the chopped rhubarb with 50g caster sugar in a baking dish and roast in the oven for 15-20 minutes until soft but holding shape. Drain excess juice and let cool completely.
To make crumble: Rub 50g cold cubed butter into flour until it resembles breadcrumbs, stir through brown sugar, spread on a baking sheet, and bake for 10-12 minutes until golden brown. Allow to cool.
Mix crushed digestive biscuits with melted butter and press firmly into the base of an 8-inch/20cm springform tin. Chill in fridge.
Beat cream cheese, icing sugar, and vanilla extract together until smooth.
Add double cream and whip until thick and holding its structure.
Fold most of the cooled roasted rhubarb through the cheesecake filling.
Spoon filling over biscuit base, smooth the top, and top with remaining rhubarb and baked crumble topping.
Refrigerate for at least 6 hours (preferably overnight) before slicing.
notes: Ensure full-fat cream cheese and double cream are used so the no-bake cheesecake sets properly.

title: Classic Duck Confit
keywords: duck confit, French, slow cooked, duck legs, crispy skin, classic
ingredients: 1½ tbsp coarse sea salt or kosher salt
500g-750g rendered duck fat (enough to cover legs)
instructions: Rub salt, garlic, crushed peppercorns, thyme, and bay leaves evenly over the duck legs.
Place legs in a dish, cover, and refrigerate to cure for 24 hours.
Preheat oven to 120°C (250°F).
Rinse salt and aromatics off duck legs thoroughly under cold water, then pat completely dry with paper towels.
Place duck legs in a small, deep baking dish or Dutch oven. Melt duck fat and pour over legs until completely submerged.
Cover dish tightly with foil or a lid and bake for 3 hours until meat is extremely tender and pulling away from the bone.
Remove legs carefully from fat.
To serve with crispy skin: Place legs skin-side down in a cold skillet over medium-low heat, cooking for 8–10 minutes until skin is deep golden brown and crispy.
notes: Strain and save the leftover duck fat in the fridge—it can be reused for cooking potatoes or roasting vegetables.

title: Pork and Chickpea Stew
keywords: pork stew, chickpeas, BBC food, comfort food, Spanish style, paprika
ingredients: 500g pork shoulder, cut into bite-sized cubes
Salt and freshly ground black pepper
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large casserole dish or Dutch oven over high heat.
Season pork shoulder pieces with salt and pepper, then brown in batches. Remove and set aside.
Lower heat to medium, add onion and garlic, and cook for 5 minutes until soft.
Stir in smoked paprika and cumin, cooking for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add canned tomatoes, chicken stock, sliced red pepper, and return browned pork to dish.
Bring to a simmer, cover with lid, lower heat, and gently cook for 1 hour.
Stir in drained chickpeas and cook uncovered for another 20–30 minutes until pork is tender and sauce thickens.
Garnish with chopped parsley and serve with crusty bread.
notes: Using pork shoulder provides much richer flavor and tenderness over quick cooking cuts during slow stewing.

title: Sous Vide Duck Confit
keywords: sous vide, duck confit, Serious Eats, precise cooking, French, duck leg
ingredients: 2 tbsp rendered duck fat (optional, legs render their own fat in bag)
instructions: Season duck legs evenly with kosher salt, black pepper, garlic, and thyme sprigs.
Place in a container or sealable bag and cure in refrigerator for 24 hours.
Rinse salt and seasonings off duck legs with cold water and pat completely dry.
Place duck legs into vacuum bags (or heavy-duty Ziploc bags) with optional tablespoon of duck fat, and seal.
Set sous vide precision cooker water bath to 68°C (155°F) for traditional tender-yet-firm texture (cook for 36 hours), OR 76°C (170°F) for fall-apart tender texture (cook for 12 hours).
Submerge sealed bags into water bath for designated time.
Remove legs from bag, wipe away liquid/gelatin, and pat skin thoroughly dry.
Crisp skin in a dry skillet over medium-low heat for 8-10 minutes, or under an oven broiler until deep brown and crackling.
notes: Sous vide eliminates the need for quarts of expensive duck fat since duck legs cook and tenderize in their own rendered fats inside the bag.

title: French Puy Lentil Ragout
keywords: puy lentils, french lentils, side dish, ragout, RecipeTin Eats, vegetarian
ingredients: 1 cup French green Puy lentils, rinsed
instructions: Heat olive oil or butter in a saucepan over medium heat.
Add diced onion, carrot, and celery (soffritto/mirepoix) and sauté for 5–7 minutes until softened.
Stir in garlic and tomato paste, cooking for 1 minute.
Add rinsed Puy lentils, stock, bay leaf, and thyme sprigs.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover with lid, and simmer gently for 25–30 minutes until lentils are tender but still hold their shape.
Remove lid and simmer 2-3 minutes if excess liquid remains.
Discard bay leaf and thyme stems.
Stir in red wine vinegar, season with salt and pepper, and garnish with fresh parsley before serving.
notes: French Puy lentils hold their shape when cooked, making them ideal for ragouts compared to brown or red lentils which break down easily.

title: Thai Basil Beef (Pad Gra Prow)
keywords: thai basil beef, pad gra prow, thai stir fry, holy basil, quick dinner, asian
ingredients: 1 lb (450g) ground beef or flank steak (sliced thinly across the grain)
2-4 Thai bird's eye chillies, finely chopped
1 cup fresh Thai basil or holy basil leaves
Fried eggs and steamed Jasmine rice, to serve
instructions: In a small bowl, mix together the soy sauce, dark soy sauce, oyster sauce, fish sauce, and sugar until dissolved.
Heat vegetable oil in a wok or large skillet over high heat.
Add minced garlic and chopped chillies, stir-frying for 15-20 seconds until fragrant.
Add the ground or sliced beef, breaking it up and searing for 2-3 minutes until browned.
Pour in the mixed sauce and stir thoroughly to coat the beef.
Turn off the heat and immediately toss in the fresh basil leaves, stirring until wilted.
Serve hot over steamed Jasmine rice topped with a crispy fried egg.
notes: Holy basil (Pad Kra Pao) offers the most authentic pepper-mint flavor, but standard Thai sweet basil or Italian basil can be substituted.

title: Slow Cooker Red Wine Beef Cheeks
keywords: beef cheeks, red wine, slow cooker, RecipeTin Eats, braised, tender beef
ingredients: 1kg (2.2 lbs) beef cheeks, trimmed of excess outer fat
1½ cups (375ml) full-bodied red wine (e.g., Cabernet Sauvignon)
instructions: Season beef cheeks generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a skillet over high heat and sear beef cheeks until deeply browned on all sides (approx 2 minutes per side). Transfer to slow cooker.
In the same skillet, saute onion, garlic, carrot, and celery for 3-4 minutes until softened.
Pour in the red wine to deglaze the pan, scraping up browned bits. Simmer for 2 minutes, then pour into slow cooker.
Add beef stock, tomato paste, bay leaves, and thyme to slow cooker.
Cover and cook on LOW for 8 hours (or HIGH for 5 hours) until beef is melt-in-your-mouth tender.
Transfer beef cheeks to a plate. Strain liquid into a saucepan and simmer over medium-high heat for 10 minutes to reduce into a rich gravy.
Serve beef cheeks over mashed potatoes drizzled with the red wine sauce.
notes: Beef cheeks contain high amounts of collagen, making them exceptionally tender and juicy after a long braise.

title: Beef, Mushroom & Vegetable Pie
keywords: beef pie, mushroom pie, puff pastry, RecipeTin Eats, comfort food, meat pie
ingredients: 800g (1.8 lbs) chuck beef, cut into 2.5cm / 1-inch cubes
1 cup red wine or extra beef stock
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C/160°C fan.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a heavy Dutch oven. Season beef with salt and pepper and brown in batches. Remove and set aside.
Add remaining oil, onion, garlic, carrot, and celery; cook for 5 minutes.
Add mushrooms and cook for 3 minutes.
Stir in flour and cook for 1 minute.
Gradually whisk in red wine, beef stock, tomato paste, and Worcestershire sauce until smooth.
Return beef and accumulated juices to pot. Cover and simmer on low heat for 1 hour 15 minutes (or bake covered in oven) until beef is tender.
Transfer filling to a pie dish and let cool slightly.
Top with puff pastry sheet, trim edges, cut a vent slit in the center, and brush with egg wash.
Bake for 25-30 minutes until pastry is golden and puffed.
notes: Letting the filling cool before topping with pastry prevents the dough from melting and becoming soggy.

title: Ultimate Baked Mac and Cheese
keywords: mac and cheese, baked macaroni, RecipeTin Eats, cheese sauce, comfort food
ingredients: 2 cups shredded Gruyere or Gruyere-style cheese
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C/160°C fan.
Cook macaroni pasta in salted boiling water for 1 minute LESS than package directions (al dente). Drain and toss with a splash of oil to prevent sticking.
Melt butter in a large saucepan over medium heat. Add flour and cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Slowly pour in milk and cream while whisking continuously until smooth.
Cook sauce for 3-5 minutes until thickened enough to coat the back of a spoon.
Remove sauce from heat. Add garlic powder, onion powder, cayenne, salt, pepper, and 3 cups of the combined shredded cheeses. Stir until melted.
Fold cooked macaroni into the cheese sauce.
Pour half the macaroni into a baking dish, sprinkle over half of the remaining cheese, top with remaining macaroni, and finish with the last layer of cheese.
Bake for 20-25 minutes until bubbly and golden on top.
notes: Shred your own cheese from blocks; pre-shredded packaged cheeses contain anti-caking agents that hinder smooth melting.

title: Five-Spice Duck Noodles
keywords: five spice, duck noodles, Waitrose, asian noodles, stir fry, quick meal
ingredients: 1 bunch spring onions, sliced lengthwise into matchsticks
1 red pepper, deseeded and sliced thinly
100g pak choi or tenderstem broccoli, sliced
instructions: Score the skin of the duck breasts in a criss-cross pattern without cutting into the meat. Season both sides with salt and five-spice powder.
Place duck breasts skin-side down in a cold, dry skillet. Turn heat to medium and cook for 8-10 minutes until fat renders out and skin is crispy.
Flip duck breasts over and cook for another 3-5 minutes. Remove from heat and let rest on a cutting board.
Meanwhile, cook egg noodles according to package instructions, drain, and toss with sesame oil.
Pour off all but 1 tbsp of duck fat from the skillet. Add spring onions, red pepper, and pak choi, stir-frying for 2-3 minutes.
Stir in soy sauce, hoisin sauce, sweet chilli sauce, and drained noodles, tossing until hot and well-coated.
Slice the rested duck breast thinly.
Divide noodles between bowls and top with sliced five-spice duck.
notes: Starting the duck skin-side down in a cold pan allows maximum fat rendering for extra crispy skin.

title: Juicy Skillet Pork Chops
keywords: pork chops, skillet, Inspired Taste, pan seared, easy dinner, quick pork
ingredients: 4 bone-in or boneless pork chops (approx 1 inch thick)
Salt and freshly cracked black pepper
instructions: Pat pork chops dry with paper towels.
Mix garlic powder, onion powder, dried thyme, paprika, 1 tsp salt, and ½ tsp pepper in a small bowl.
Rub spice mixture over both sides of the pork chops.
Heat olive oil in a heavy skillet (preferably cast iron) over medium-high heat until hot.
Add pork chops and sear undisturbed for 3-4 minutes until a deep golden crust forms.
Flip chops over, then add butter, smashed garlic, and fresh rosemary sprigs to the skillet.
Spoon melted garlic butter continuously over the pork chops as they cook for another 3-4 minutes.
Remove chops when internal temperature reaches 63°C (145°F). Rest for 5 minutes before serving.
notes: Using thicker-cut chops (1 inch+) prevents the meat from drying out during high-heat pan searing.

title: Classic Cottage Pie
keywords: cottage pie, beef mince, mashed potato, BBC Good Food, comfort food, British
instructions: Heat oil in a large saucepan over medium heat. Cook onion, carrots, and celery for 5 minutes until soft.
Add minced beef and cook for 6-8 minutes until browned, breaking it up with a spoon.
Stir in flour and tomato purée, cooking for 1 minute.
Pour in beef stock, Worcestershire sauce, and thyme. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer uncovered for 20 minutes until sauce thickens.
Meanwhile, boil potatoes in salted water for 15-20 minutes until tender. Drain and mash with butter and milk until smooth.
Preheat oven to 200°C/180°C fan/gas 6.
Transfer beef filling into an ovenproof baking dish. Spread mashed potato evenly over the top and ruffle with a fork.
Sprinkle optional cheddar cheese on top.
Bake for 25-30 minutes until golden brown and bubbling.
notes: Ruffling the top of the mashed potatoes with a fork creates crispy ridges during baking.

title: Perfect Roast Beef
keywords: roast beef, Jamie Oliver, Sunday roast, sirloin, ribeye, classic roast
ingredients: 1.5kg top round, sirloin, or ribeye beef joint
2 carrots, washed and chopped into large chunks
2 celery sticks, chopped into large chunks
1 bulb garlic, broken into unpeeled cloves
1 small bunch fresh thyme, rosemary, or sage
instructions: Remove beef from refrigerator 30 minutes before cooking to allow it to reach room temperature.
Preheat oven to 240°C/460°F/gas 9.
Pile onions, carrots, celery, garlic cloves, and fresh herbs into the center of a roasting tray and drizzle with olive oil.
Rub beef joint thoroughly with olive oil and season generously with salt and black pepper.
Place beef directly on top of the bed of vegetables in the roasting tray.
Place tray into oven and immediately turn heat down to 200°C/400°F/gas 6.
Roast for 1 hour for medium (1 hour 15 mins for medium-well, 50 mins for medium-rare).
Baste meat halfway through cooking with pan juices.
Transfer beef to a board, cover loosely with foil, and rest for at least 15-20 minutes before carving.
notes: Vegetables in the bottom of the tray elevate the meat for even cooking and make a base for gravy.

title: Easy Baked Cod
keywords: baked cod, white fish, lemon garlic butter, quick seafood, low carb, healthy
ingredients: Salt and freshly ground black pepper
Fresh chopped parsley and lemon slices, for garnish
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F) and lightly grease a baking dish.
Pat cod fillets completely dry with paper towels and place into prepared baking dish.
In a small bowl, whisk together melted butter, lemon juice, minced garlic, paprika, onion powder, salt, and pepper.
Pour lemon butter mixture evenly over cod fillets.
Bake in oven for 12-15 minutes, depending on thickness, until fish flakes easily with a fork and reaches internal temp of 63°C (145°F).
Garnish with fresh parsley and extra lemon slices before serving.
notes: Patting fish dry before baking ensures it bakes cleanly without stewing in excess water.

title: Easy Family Fish Pie
keywords: fish pie, easy fish pie, BBC Good Food, cod, salmon, mashed potato, seafood
ingredients: 1kg potatoes, peeled and cut into chunks
400g fish pie mix (salmon, cod, and smoked haddock chunks)
instructions: Boil potatoes in salted water for 15 minutes until tender. Drain and mash thoroughly with 50g butter and 50ml milk.
Melt 50g butter in a saucepan over medium heat, stir in flour, and cook for 1 minute.
Gradually whisk in 450ml milk until a smooth sauce forms. Bring to a gentle simmer and stir until thickened.
Remove sauce from heat and stir in half of the grated cheese.
Preheat oven to 200°C/180°C fan/gas 6.
Place raw fish pie mix, cooked prawns, and sweetcorn/peas into the bottom of a large baking dish.
Pour cheese sauce evenly over raw seafood and vegetables.
Spoon mashed potato over sauce layer, smoothing with a fork, and top with remaining grated cheese.
Bake for 25-30 minutes until top is golden and filling is bubbling.
notes: Using pre-packaged fish pie mix (salmon, white fish, smoked haddock) saves preparation time.

title: Slow-Cooked Mexican Lamb Birria Tacos
keywords: lamb birria, birria tacos, Mexican, slow cooked lamb, consomme, tacos
ingredients: 1.5kg shoulder or leg of lamb, bone-in or cut into chunks
3 dried guajillo chillies, stemmed and deseeded
2 dried ancho chillies, stemmed and deseeded
1-2 dried chillies de árbol (optional for heat)
Corn tortillas, shredded cheese, chopped cilantro, and diced onion to serve
instructions: Toast dried chillies in a hot dry skillet for 1-2 minutes until fragrant, then soak in boiling water for 15 minutes to soften.
Transfer soaked chillies to a blender with onion, garlic, tomatoes, vinegar, oregano, cumin, cinnamon, and a splash of soaking water. Blend until completely smooth.
Season lamb with salt and pepper. Brown in a Dutch oven or large heavy pot over medium-high heat.
Pour blended chilli sauce and lamb stock over the lamb.
Cover tightly and simmer on low heat for 3.5 to 4 hours (or slow cook on Low for 8 hours) until meat falls off the bone.
Shred lamb, discarding bones and fat, and strain excess braising liquid into a bowl for dipping (consomé).
Dip corn tortillas in top layer of fat from consomé, fry in a pan, fill with shredded lamb and cheese, fold, and cook until crisp. Serve with consomé for dipping.
notes: Dip tortillas in the fat skimmed off the braising liquid before frying to get authentic birria crispness and color.

title: Slow-Cooked Chicken Tinga Tacos
keywords: chicken tinga, tacos, slow cooker, Mexican, shredded chicken, chipotle
ingredients: 2-3 chipotle peppers in adobo sauce, chopped, plus 2 tbsp sauce
Small warm corn or flour tortillas, avocado, cotija/feta cheese, and lime wedges to serve
instructions: Heat olive oil in a pan over medium heat and cook sliced onions for 5 minutes until softened.
Add garlic, chopped chipotle peppers, adobo sauce, oregano, and cumin; stir for 1 minute.
Add chopped tomatoes and chicken stock, bring to a simmer, then transfer mixture into slow cooker (or keep in pot if slow cooking on stove).
Nestle raw chicken thighs into sauce, cover, and cook on LOW for 6 hours or HIGH for 3.5–4 hours.
Remove chicken thighs, shred meat using two forks, and return shredded chicken to sauce.
Simmer uncovered for 10-15 minutes so chicken absorbs sauce and mixture thickens.
Spoon chicken tinga into warmed tortillas and top with avocado slices, crumbled cheese, and lime juice.
notes: Adjust the number of chipotle peppers to control spice levels without sacrificing smoky flavor.

title: Slow Cooker Korean Beef
keywords: korean beef, slow cooker, Taming Twins, soy sauce, sesame oil, easy dinner
ingredients: 700g braising beef or chuck steak, cut into bite-sized pieces
2 tbsp gochujang (Korean chilli paste) or sriracha
2 tbsp cornflour mixed with 2 tbsp cold water
Sesame seeds and sliced spring onions, to garnish
instructions: In slow cooker bowl, whisk together soy sauce, brown sugar, sesame oil, garlic, ginger, and gochujang.
Add beef pieces to slow cooker and toss to coat in sauce.
Cover and cook on LOW for 6-7 hours or HIGH for 3-4 hours until beef is tender.
Stir cornflour slurry into slow cooker, cover, and cook on HIGH for 15-20 minutes until sauce thickens to a glossy glaze.
Garnish with sesame seeds and sliced spring onions. Serve over steamed rice.
notes: Gochujang gives an authentic Korean flavor balance of sweet, salty, and mild spice.

title: One Pot Chicken Orzo
keywords: chicken orzo, one pot, Don't Go Bacon My Heart, easy pasta, weeknight dinner
ingredients: 500g boneless skinless chicken thighs, cut into bite-sized pieces
½ cup heavy cream or double cream
instructions: Heat olive oil and butter in a large skillet or shallow Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Season chicken pieces with Italian seasoning, salt, and pepper. Brown in skillet for 5 minutes until golden; remove and set aside.
Add diced onion to skillet and cook for 3-4 minutes until softened, then stir in garlic and tomato paste for 1 minute.
Stir in dry orzo pasta to coat in pan oils.
Pour in chicken stock, bring to a simmer, then return chicken and juices to pan.
Cover, reduce heat to low, and simmer for 8-10 minutes, stirring occasionally to stop orzo sticking, until pasta is tender.
Stir in heavy cream, grated Parmesan, and baby spinach until spinach wilts and sauce becomes creamy. Serve immediately.
notes: Stir the orzo regularly during simmering to prevent it from sticking to the bottom of the pan.

title: Sous Vide Barbecue Pulled Pork Shoulder
keywords: sous vide, pulled pork, pork shoulder, barbecue, Serious Eats, slow cook
ingredients: 2.5kg–3kg bone-in or boneless pork shoulder (pork butt)
Barbecue sauce of choice, to serve
instructions: Combine brown sugar, salt, smoked paprika, black pepper, garlic powder, onion powder, and mustard powder to create dry rub.
Rub spice mixture generously over entire pork shoulder.
Seal pork shoulder in a large vacuum bag (or heavy-duty Ziploc bag using water displacement method), adding liquid smoke if using.
Set sous vide water bath to 74°C (165°F) for traditional shreddable pork, or 65°C (149°F) for firmer sliceable/shreddable pork.
Submerge sealed bag in water bath and cook for 24 hours.
Remove pork from bag, reserving bag juices for sauce if desired, and pat skin/surface dry.
To finish: Bake in a 150°C (300°F) oven or smoke on low heat grill for 1.5–2 hours until a dark outer bark forms.
Shred pork using two forks and toss with barbecue sauce.
notes: Finish in oven or smoker after sous vide cooking to recreate a authentic crispy exterior bark.

title: Slow Cooked Lamb with Orzo (Giouvetsi)
keywords: lamb orzo, giouvetsi, Greek, slow cooked lamb, braised, A Fork & A Pencil
ingredients: 1kg lamb shoulder or leg, cut into large chunks
Grated mizithra or feta cheese, to serve
instructions: Preheat oven to 160°C/140°C fan/gas 3.
Heat olive oil in a large ovenproof Dutch oven. Season lamb chunks with salt and pepper and sear until browned on all sides. Remove lamb.
Add onion and garlic to pot, cooking for 5 minutes until soft.
Stir in tomato paste, red wine, chopped tomatoes, cinnamon stick, and bay leaves. Simmer for 2 minutes to reduce wine.
Return lamb to pot and add stock. Cover tightly and bake in oven for 1.5 to 2 hours until lamb is extremely tender.
Remove pot from oven, stir in dried orzo pasta and an extra splash of hot water if liquid is low.
Cover and return to oven for 20-25 minutes until orzo is cooked through and tender.
Discard cinnamon stick and bay leaves. Serve warm topped with grated feta cheese.
notes: Orzo absorbs the rich braising liquid while baking, making the pasta deeply savory.

title: Genuine Cornish Pasty
keywords: cornish pasty, Cornish Pasty Association, traditional, beef, potato, swede, pastry
ingredients: 350g good quality beef side skirt or chuck steak, finely diced
200g swede (yellow turnip), peeled and finely diced
Salt and plenty of freshly cracked black pepper
instructions: Rub butter and shortening/lard into flour with salt until it resembles fine breadcrumbs, then gradually add cold water to form a firm dough. Wrap and chill in fridge for 30 minutes.
Divide pastry into 4 equal portions and roll each into a circle approx 20cm (8 inches) wide.
Layer raw diced swede, potato, beef, and chopped onion in the center of each pastry circle.
Season filling generously with salt and black pepper.
Dampen pastry edges with water, pull sides up over filling to meet in the middle, and crimp edges firmly together to seal.
Place pasties on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper and brush thoroughly with egg wash.
Bake in a preheated oven at 200°C (400°F) for 20 minutes, then lower heat to 160°C (320°F) and bake for a further 30 minutes until golden.
notes: Authentic Cornish pasties use raw filling ingredients that cook completely inside the sealed pastry crust during baking.

title: Baked Spiced Cod with Garlic and Lemon
keywords: baked cod, spiced fish, garlic lemon, Bute Island Seafoodie, easy seafood, low carb
ingredients: Fresh chopped parsley and lemon slices, to serve
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F).
Pat cod fillets completely dry with paper towels and place into a greased baking dish.
In a small bowl, whisk together melted butter, olive oil, minced garlic, paprika, cumin, coriander, cayenne pepper, lemon zest, and lemon juice.
Season cod fillets with salt and pepper, then spoon spice mixture evenly over each fillet.
Bake for 12–15 minutes until cod is opaque and flakes easily with a fork.
Garnish with fresh parsley and serve with additional lemon slices.
notes: Use fresh cod fillets of uniform thickness to ensure even baking time.

title: How to Wet Brine a Turkey
keywords: turkey, wet brine, Thanksgiving, ratio, poultry, salt water

ratioFormula.salt: 1 cup kosher salt (or ½ cup table salt)

timingRules.postBrineRest: 30–60 minutes at room temperature before roasting

equipmentRequired: Food-safe bucket, brining bag, or large pot
ingredients: 1 cup kosher salt (or ½ cup table salt)
Optional aromatics: 1 tbsp black peppercorns, 3-4 crushed garlic cloves, 3-4 sprigs fresh rosemary/thyme, 2 bay leaves, sliced citrus fruits
instructions: In a large stockpot, combine 1 cup kosher salt, brown sugar, optional aromatics, and 1 gallon of water.
Bring the water to a simmer over medium-high heat, stirring until the salt and sugar completely dissolve.
Remove from heat and allow the brine to cool to room temperature, then stir in the 1 gallon of ice water to chill completely.
Remove the giblets and neck from the turkey cavity.
Place the turkey breast-side down into a large pot, food-safe bucket, or brining bag, and pour the cooled brine over the turkey until fully submerged.
Refrigerate and brine for 12 to 24 hours (do not exceed 24 hours).
Remove the turkey from the brine, rinse thoroughly with cold water, and pat dry with paper towels inside and out.
Allow the turkey to sit at room temperature for 30 to 60 minutes before roasting as desired.
notes: Food Safety Note: Never leave poultry in wet brine past 24 hours to prevent texturing issues, and ensure liquid temperature stays under 40°F (4°C) throughout.
